  2371      Section 351.503(c) Consideration of performance includes language 
  2372  currently in Sec.  351.504(b) but modifies this language by removing 
  2373  the reference to ``additional retention service credit'' (i.e., credit 
  2374  for performance will no longer be added to an employee's length of 
  2375  service). Performance will now be the primary basis for rating 
  2376  employees within each tenure group. Performance will be measured based 
  2377  on performance credit, i.e., the total of each employee's summary level 
  2378  ratings for the employee's three most recent ratings of record for 
  2379  performance consistent with Sec.  351.503(a), which will then be 
  2380  augmented by additional credit for veterans' preference status as set 
  2381  forth in Sec.  351.504.
  2382      New paragraph Sec.  351.503(d) Single rating pattern describes how 
  2383  agencies list employees who have been covered under the same rating 
  2384  pattern of summary levels during the 4-year period prior to the date of 
  2385  issuance of the reduction in force notice or the agency-established 
  2386  cutoff date. Paragraph (d) provides that, for employees covered under a 
  2387  summary level appraisal system in which the highest summary level is a 
  2388  level ``3'' rating (i.e., a pattern A (`pass/fail'), or pattern D 
  2389  system authorized under 430.208(d) prior to the final rule prescribed 
  2390  at 91 FR 41521), the agency may, in its sole and exclusive discretion, 
  2391  give additional credit for employees who have documented exceptional 
  2392  performance to give more weight to certain performance-related actions 
  2393  than others for purposes of listing some level ``3'' employees ahead of 
  2394  other employees on a retention register. Evidence of exceptional 
  2395  performance may include documentation showing an agency has awarded: an 
  2396  employee with the highest Agency or Departmental award (such as a 
  2397  Secretary's or Chairman's award), a special act or service award, a 
  2398  quality step increase (QSI), or other performance awards or bonuses 
  2399  (e.g., a ``time-off'' award for demonstrated performance above 
  2400  expectations).
  2401      Commenter 0683 expressed concern that this could ``create[] a 
  2402  system in which the same level of actual performance could yield 
  2403  materially different retention outcomes depending on which agency the 
  2404  employee works for and what award budget was available.'' OPM 
  2405  disagrees. Instead, it believes this change will provide a method by 
  2406  which an agency may make meaningful distinctions among employees in a 
  2407  pattern A performance appraisal program (i.e., the highest summary 
  2408  level rating is a ``3'' or satisfactory) who have documented 
  2409  performance above expectations in these appraisal systems. It thus 
  2410  directly addresses Commenter 0683's concern that existing performance 
  2411  appraisal systems do not always meaningfully differentiate relative 
  2412  performance, along with Commenter 0683's concerns regarding variations 
  2413  in rating patterns across agencies.
  2414      For example, the employees below are covered under a three-summary 
  2415  level pattern as described in 5 CFR 430.208(e). Their agency has an 
  2416  established policy of providing enhanced performance credit by 
  2417  assigning 7 points for agency awards, 5 points for organizational 
  2418  awards, and 4 points for various performance awards. (An agency award 
  2419  is designated by ``A''; a component-level award is designated by ``O''; 
  2420  and a performance award or QSI is designated by ``P''.) Their ratings 
  2421  and totals are:
  2422  
  2423  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2424                                                                                    Assigned
  2425            Employee                Ratings       Performance       Award(s)       values for          Total
  2426                                                    credit                           awards
  2427  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2428  Carol.......................           3/3/3           3/3/3  O/O/A..........           5/5/7     3+3+3+5+5+7=26
  2429  Alice.......................           3/3/3           3/3/3  A/-/P..........           7/0/4       3+3+3+7+4=20
  2430  Bill........................           2/3/3           0/3/3  -/-/P..........           0/0/4     0+3+3+0+0+4=10
  2431  
  2432  [[Page 49198]]
  2433  
  2434   
  2435  Fred........................           3/3/3           3/3/3  -/-/-..........           0/0/0      3+3+3+0+0+0=9
  2436  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2437  
  2438      New paragraph Sec.  351.503(e) Multiple rating patterns addresses 
  2439  situations in which an agency has employees in a competitive area who 
  2440  have ratings of record under more than one pattern of summary levels, 
  2441  as described in 5 CFR 430.208(e). An agency may, in its sole and 
  2442  exclusive discretion, choose to provide enhanced performance credit to 
  2443  employees under disparate pattern summary levels. It may do so by 
  2444  transmuting or assigning an employee a higher summary level rating than 
  2445  what he or she received under a previous rating system when there is 
  2446  documented evidence of exceptional or higher-level performance 
  2447  consistent with the criteria in revised Sec.  351.503(d).
  2448      In addition, for an employee who goes from an appraisal system 
  2449  which uses a higher pattern of summary levels to a lower one (e.g., an 
  2450  employee who goes from a 5 summary level appraisal program to a two 
  2451  level system (i.e., pass/fail system)), an agency may adopt policies 
  2452  which would allow employees with ratings above the highest summary 
  2453  level of the lower pattern system to be listed ahead of any employee on 
  2454  the retention register who does not have documented evidence of 
  2455  exceptional performance as described above. This method allows agencies 
  2456  to adopt policies that would prevent exceptional performers from being 
  2457  disadvantaged because they may be covered under two or more patterns of 
  2458  summary rating levels which may not make meaningful distinctions for 
  2459  performance among employees. Further, Sec.  351.503 will require RIF 
  2460  performance ratings and assigned summary levels, including adjustments, 
  2461  to be uniformly and consistently applied within the competitive area 
  2462  and consistent with the agency's implementing issuances. Where an 
  2463  agency elects to assign additional performance credit, the agency must 
  2464  specify and document the criteria in advance and make them available 
  2465  for review.
  2466      Paragraph (f) of Sec.  351.503 describes how an agency should 
  2467  factor performance ratings into the RIF process when an employee does 
  2468  not have three actual ratings of record during the 4-year period prior 
  2469  to the date of issuance of RIF notices, or the 4-year period prior to 
  2470  the agency-established cut-off date. It uses the modal rating concept 
  2471  for employees with no ratings during the 4-year period prior to the 
  2472  RIF, as currently found in Sec.  351.504(c)(1), but modifies the 
  2473  current provisions by removing the reference to ``additional retention 
  2474  service credit.''
  2475      Section 351.504 Veterans' preference defines how veterans' 
  2476  preference will be applied in a RIF in both the competitive and 
  2477  excepted services. Each preference eligible employee with a compensable 
  2478  service-connected disability of 30 percent or more will receive an 
  2479  additional 5 points added to their performance credit, while every 
  2480  other preference eligible employee will receive an additional 3 points 
  2481  added to their performance credit. ``Preference eligibles'' is defined 
  2482  in 5 U.S.C. 2108(3) to include not only veterans, but also certain 
  2483  close family members of deceased or service-disabled veterans. Non-
  2484  preference eligible employees do not receive any additional points 
  2485  added to their performance score.
  2486      Commenter 0660 asserted, without any additional information, that 
  2487  ``the proposed rules are vague and unclear as to exactly how 
  2488  performance and veterans' issues are to be determined,'' but does not 
  2489  indicate in what manner the proposed rule is vague or unclear, 
  2490  providing no supporting information whatsoever. Commenter 0660 
  2491  contended that ``[t]he proposed regulation will make it likely that the 
  2492  classifications will result in numerous appeals challenging the order 
  2493  and create chaos in their implementation as a result,'' but failed to 
  2494  explain how the new regulation is more complicated than the current 
  2495  rules.
  2496      OPM disagrees with Commenter 0660's assertions. The current rules 
  2497  require agencies to categorize employees based on tenure group and 
  2498  veterans' preference subgroup. Employees are ranked first by tenure 
  2499  group I, II, III; then within each tenure group by veterans' preference 
  2500  subgroup AD, A, B; and only then by years of service as augmented by 
  2501  performance credit, starting with the earliest service date. Agencies 
  2502  then prepare an ``adjusted SCD'' calculation where extra years of 
  2503  service are added to an employee's actual service computation date. 
  2504  That means current RIF ordering is not a simple comparison of Employee 
  2505  A's performance against Employee B's performance. Agencies must first 
  2506  place employees into tenure groups, then veterans' preference 
  2507  subgroups, then calculate adjusted service dates. Performance affects 
  2508  ranking only inside the employee's already-determined tenure/veterans' 
  2509  preference category.
  2510      Agencies then must undergo multiple rounds of complicated bumping 
  2511  and retreating before arriving at a final retention register. Notably, 
  2512  ``bump and retreat'' can create a chain. If Employee A bumps Employee 
  2513  B, then Employee B is released from that competitive level, and the 
  2514  agency must determine whether Employee B has his or her own bump or 
  2515  retreat right. This process is highly burdensome and prone to errors.
  2516      This rule replaces the current rules with a streamlined system that 
  2517  eliminates the need for multiple, complicated rounds of bump and 
  2518  retreat, replacing it with a straightforward comparison of employee 
  2519  performance as augmented by veterans' preference, with ties broken by 
  2520  tenure and length of service. Further, OPM's new rules are simpler 
  2521  because they eliminate the most confusing features of the current 
  2522  rules: using performance to manufacture an adjusted service computation 
  2523  date and complicated bump-and-retreat procedures.
  2524      This rule addresses that problem by making performance credit more 
  2525  transparent and direct: Level 5 ratings receive 7 points, Level 4 
  2526  ratings receive 5 points, Level 3 ratings receive 3 points, and Level 1 
  2527  or 2 ratings receive no points. Veterans' preference is then added to 
  2528  that performance credit.
  2529      This rule's use of defined point values--Level 5 = 7 points, Level 
  2530  4 = 5 points, Level 3 = 3 points, and Level 1 or 2 = 0 points--also 
  2531  makes the RIF calculation easier to understand and audit than an 
  2532  artificial performance-adjusted SCD. As Commenter 0687 noted, this 
  2533  reform simplifies the composition of retention registers.
  2534      In addition, this rule does not change the basic record-keeping 
  2535  requirements in current Sec.  351.505 (renumbered to Sec.  351.506) or 
  2536  the notice requirements in Sec.  351.802, except to conform their 
  2537  provisions to other changes made in this rulemaking. Thus, OPM does not 
  2538  agree with Commenter 0678's assertion that the rule ``reduces notice 
  2539  and transparency'' regarding RIFs. Instead, OPM agrees with Commenter 
  2540  0687, who noted that the revisions ``simplify[ ] the composition of 
  2541  retention registers . . . such that retention standing is faster to 
  2542  compute, more transparent, and more equitably applied.''
  2543  
  2544  [[Page 49199]]
  2545  
  2546      In the proposed rule, OPM provided order of retention examples. 
  2547  Commenter 0680 points out correctly that some of the tables 
  2548  illustrating the operation of the proposed rule contained errors, as 
  2549  they incorrectly ranked employees in a higher tenure subgroup ahead of 
  2550  employees with a greater performance credit. OPM is therefore 
  2551  correcting these examples below. OPM is also publishing further 
  2552  examples of how retention standing will work under the new regulations 
  2553  to aid with administration of the new rules.
  2554      OPM disagrees with Commenter 0680 that these inadvertent errors 
  2555  show a lack of reasoned decision-making, that the new rules increase 
  2556  the risk of mistakes, or that OPM or agencies are unprepared to 
  2557  administer the new rules. Such a correction is consistent with ordinary 
  2558  rulemaking practice: agencies often revise, add, delete, or correct 
  2559  examples to conform them to the operative regulatory standard or to 
  2560  respond to comments.\16\ The binding rule is the regulatory text, which 
  2561  provides that employees are ranked by performance credit as augmented 
  2562  by veterans' preference, with tenure subgroup and service computation 
  2563  date used as tie-breakers. The proposed rule text clearly stated that, 
  2564  within each tenure group, employees are ranked by performance credit as 
  2565  augmented by veterans' preference, and only when employees have the 
  2566  same augmented performance credit are they further ranked by tenure 
  2567  subgroup and then by length of service.
  2568      Indeed, OPM believes the new RIF formula is much simpler to 
  2569  understand and apply than the current formula, as it involves a simple 
  2570  calculation of performance credits adjusted for veterans' status, with 
  2571  tenure subgroup and length of service serving as tiebreakers. The 
  2572  current system, by contrast, involves a multi-layered system where 
  2573  employees were sorted into three tenure groups, with veterans' status 
  2574  subgroups within each tenure group, with employees then further sorted 
  2575  by service computation date that is adjusted based on performance. That 
  2576  process required agencies to translate performance into years, average 
  2577  the credited years, round where necessary, and then move the employee's 
  2578  service date backward to create an ``adjusted SCD.'' That made the 
  2579  register harder to understand because the service computation date was 
  2580  not the employee's actual service date, but an artificial service date 
  2581  reflecting both service and performance. Further, agencies were then 
  2582  required to engage in complicated ``bump and retreat'' exercises 
  2583  between employees in different tenure groups, often encompassing 
  2584  multiple rounds of RIF competition governed by detailed rules that were 
  2585  understood by very few beyond a very small group of Federal HR 
  2586  specialists and consultants.
  2587      Under this rule, by contrast, performance remains a score that 
  2588  corresponds to direct numerical values, augmented by consistent 
  2589  numerical values for veterans' preference. Thus, the new rules will 
  2590  likely result in far fewer errors than the old rules. They are also 
  2591  easier and more streamlined, making them easier to apply and understand 
  2592  by both HR offices and Federal employees. Employees who inspect the 
  2593  register will be much more likely to understand how their retention 
  2594  standing was calculated and be able to spot errors.
  2595      Several commenters agree that the new regulations are simpler than 
  2596  the current ones. Commenter 0687 noted that the new rule simplifies the 
  2597  composition of retention registers and the application of assignment 
  2598  rights, versus the current complicated ``bump and retreat'' process. 
  2599  Commenter 0685 noted that the benefits of OPM's simplification of RIF 
  2600  rules are ``substantial and should not be understated,'' and that ``the 
  2601  proposal's effort to simplify the RIF framework represents a meaningful 
  2602  and constructive reform.''
  2603      The following examples illustrate and contrast the impact of 
  2604  performance ratings of record and their summary levels on a retention 
  2605  register under the current rules and this final rule. Consider the

Q13 candidates here:
- Lines 2272-2281: "The competitive service tenure group will consist of all competitive service employees ... who are not (as of the date of the RIF notice) serving an initial probationary period or a temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less under 5 CFR part 316." Text 351.502(a)(3): subgroup II excludes "a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316" (not time-limited) and 351.202(d)(2)(iii) same. Preamble says "temporary or time-limited" for competitive service. Inaccurate; another passage lines 2287-2290 says "temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less" (also inaccurate—text says temporary only). Hmm, multiple preamble statements use "temporary or time-limited" / "temporary or term" while text says temporary only. Q13 item.
- Lines 2282-2286: "competitive service tenure subgroup I will include each career employee in the competitive service who, as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice, is not serving an initial probationary period." Text 351.502(a)(2) says "as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice." Consistent.
- Lines 2287-2290: "Competitive service tenure subgroup II will consist of every other competitive service employee who, as of the date of the RIF notice, is not serving an initial probationary period or a temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less." Text uses "date employee receives" and "temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D"; preamble says "date of the RIF notice" and "temporary or term appointment." Inaccurate on both. Another passage lines 2282-2286 states receipt correctly for subgroup I. Q13 items.
- Lines 2301-2304: "Excepted service tenure subgroup II will consist of all other career employees ... who are not serving a trial period or a temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less." Text 351.502(b)(3): "not serving a trial period and who are not serving in a temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less." consistent.
- Lines 2309-2318: "Generally, the three most recent ratings of record received during the 4-year period prior to the date of issuance of reduction in force notices may be considered" — text says "must be based on the employee's three most recent ... ratings of record received during the 4-year period prior to the date of issuance..." "may be considered" vs "must be based" — preamble uses permissive language. Could be Q13 item? Maybe not; it later says "Agencies will list ... based on ... three most recent..." (lines 2340-2344) correctly.
- Lines 2345-2350: "each preference eligible veteran ... while every other preference eligible veteran..." Text 351.504(a) applies to "each preference eligible employee" / "Every other preference eligible employee" — preamble says "veteran" rather than "employee." This is a real difference in category of employee: preference eligibles include certain family members, not just veterans. Preamble later at 2481-2483 correctly says "'Preference eligibles' is defined in 5 U.S.C. 2108(3) to include not only veterans, but also certain close family members..." So Q13 item: preamble at 49197 says "preference eligible veteran" while text 351.504(a) says "preference eligible employee"; another passage correctly notes non-veteran preference eligibles.
- Lines 2382-2390: "for employees covered under a summary level appraisal system in which the highest summary level is a level '3' rating ... agency may ... give additional credit for employees who have documented exceptional performance..." Text 351.503(d): "an agency may, in its sole and exclusive discretion, assign additional points for performance for employees covered under a summary level appraisal system in which the highest summary level is a level '3' rating..." consistent.
- Lines 2466-2474: "Paragraph (f) ... uses the modal rating concept for employees with no ratings during the 4-year period prior to the RIF, as currently found in Sec. 351.504(c)(1)..." Text 351.503(f)(1) says "modal rating as defined in Sec. 351.203." Preamble says current provision in 351.504(c)(1), not relevant.
- Lines 2534-2537: "this rule does not change the basic record-keeping requirements in current Sec. 351.505 (renumbered to Sec. 351.506) or the notice requirements in Sec. 351.802, except to conform their provisions to other changes..." But final 351.506 adds new paragraph (d) sentence and changes; 351.802 changes. "Does not change basic record-keeping requirements" maybe still okay? It does add sentence. Could be Q13 item? Maybe not.
- Lines 2546-2552: preamble acknowledges proposed examples errors, but Q13 is preamble vs regulatory text, not proposal vs final.

Need continue Subpart E preamble for 351.505-507, lines 2648-2835.

tools.name: fr_search

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".
query.title: Query

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.
doc_type.title: Doc Type

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).
pres_type.title: Pres Type

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.
cfr.title: Cfr

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_grep

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.
pattern.title: Pattern

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).
context.title: Context

tools.description: Regex search inside one document's full text. Shows the lines of each match with line numbers, context lines and the FR page of each match. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

tools.name: fr_text
tools.description: Read a document's full text by line range, with line numbers. [[Page N]] markers give FR page numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

answer.description: Direct answer to each lettered part, in order, labelled (a), (b), ...
answer.title: Answer

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.
basis.title: Basis

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

Q13 candidate: Line 2680-2683 says retention factors order: "Tenure | Performance based on total of summary levels | Vets Pref | Service Computation Date." But text 351.501(b)-(c): performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference is one combined factor; then tenure subgroup, then SCD. The preamble lists Vets Pref as a separate factor after performance, which might suggest veterans' preference considered separately, but actually points are added to performance credit. However, the example totals show +3 included. Later passages say performance as augmented by veterans' preference. Could be Q13 item: preamble at 49200 says factors considered "Tenure | Performance based on total of employee's summary levels | Vets Pref | Service Computation Date," whereas text 351.501(b) uses "performance credit ... as augmented by veterans' preference" and 351.501(c) tie-breakers tenure subgroup and SCD. Another passage at 2561-2567 states correctly. Strong-ish.

Also line 2662-2666: "Assume same group... Emma receives additional performance credit based on status as a veteran with a compensable service-connected disability" — but Emma in table has 18 (16+2?), wait table shows Emma 3/4/4 = 3+5+5=13 +5=18. Yes, +5. The narrative says "additional performance credit" without specifying 5. Fine.

Also Example 4 final at 2713-2717: Harper 21, Imani 17, Jorge 16, Kai 12, Lena 9. Order correct. But note line 2724-2725: "If two employees must be released from this competitive level, the agency would release Lena first, then Kai." Correct.

Line 2750-2755: "Kai moves from first under current rules to fourth under this final rule because veterans' preference and tenure no longer control ahead of performance; veterans' preference adds points..." consistent.

Line 2765: Priya "4/3/missing ... 12 + 3 = 15" correct. Good.

Line 2807-2813: "OPM is modifying Sec. 351.506(c) to make these provisions consistent with changes in Sec. 351.505." Actually 351.505 is length of service; 351.506(c) records. Maybe should say 351.503/351.504? Hmm. It says "changes in Sec. 351.505" perhaps wrong cross-reference; but not necessarily a statement about what rule provides. Could be Q13 item if it describes modification incorrectly.

Line 2824-2833: 351.805(b) correct.

Continue Subpart F preamble 2835-3050. This includes 351.605, 351.606, 351.608.

  2835  E. Part 351, Subpart F: Furloughs, Abolishment of Competitive Area, 
  2836  USERRA Rights, and Exceptions
  2837  
  2838      OPM is modifying Sec.  351.601 for consistency with how retention 
  2839  standing is to be calculated under Subpart E of part 351. OPM is also 
  2840  modifying Sec.  351.602 to remove the prohibition on retaining an 
  2841  employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment in a 
  2842  competitive level while releasing a competing employee from that level. 
  2843  OPM did not receive significant adverse comments on these provisions 
  2844  and is finalizing them.
  2845  1. RIF Furloughs
  2846      In the proposed rule, OPM proposed to modify its regulations in 
  2847  Sec.  351.604 regarding furloughs of more than 30 consecutive calendar 
  2848  days (or more than 22 workdays if done on a discontinuous basis over a 
  2849  period not exceeding 1 year) to remove the requirement that agencies 
  2850  furlough employees based on retention standing and recall employees to 
  2851  duty from furlough based on retention standing.
  2852      Commenter 0687 opposed these changes, contending that they had ``no 
  2853  obvious use case and could create mechanisms for abuse.'' Commenter 
  2854  0687 noted that agencies typically do not engage in unpaid furloughs of 
  2855  any length, whether greater or less than 30 days, and that OPM's 
  2856  proposed revision would create risks that agencies could use long 
  2857  furloughs to circumvent normal RIF procedures. Commenter 0687 therefore 
  2858  contended that the risks of this new provision outweigh the benefits. 
  2859  Commenter 0117 similarly expressed concern that agencies could use 
  2860  long-term unpaid furloughs to avoid following retention order 
  2861  requirements. OPM agrees that its proposed changes to Sec.  351.604 
  2862  warrant further consideration and has chosen not to finalize them.
  2863  2. Abolishment of a Competitive Area
  2864      In this rule, OPM is renaming Sec.  351.605 as Abolishment of a 
  2865  competitive area to more accurately describe its purpose. The revised 
  2866  section explains that the appropriate use of this provision is when an 
  2867  agency is abolishing all positions (including the positions of 
  2868  employees otherwise excluded from RIF competition under Sec.  
  2869  351.202(d)) in a competitive area within 180 days. It further explains 
  2870  that, because all positions in the competitive area will be eliminated, 
  2871  an agency is not required to release competing employees in order of 
  2872  retention standing.
  2873      As the D.C. Circuit explained in upholding an earlier version of 
  2874  this provision, when all employees in a competitive area will be 
  2875  released within a relatively short time, ``it is certainly reasonable 
  2876  to conclude that it would be a waste of resources for an agency to be 
  2877  forced to perform detailed seniority and performance calculations 
  2878  solely to construct a rank ordering of employees' retention rights when 
  2879  those rights are of such little value.'' AFGE v. OPM, 821 F.2d at 766 
  2880  n. 4. Thus, OPM was ``within its authority to conclude that under those 
  2881  limited circumstances, no effect is `due.' '' Id. With performance now 
  2882  the main consideration governing RIF retention, the same considerations 
  2883  apply: it does not make sense to require agencies to perform detailed 
  2884  seniority and performance calculations to construct a rank ordering of 
  2885  employees that will have no substantive effect on their retention 
  2886  rights.
  2887      In this final rule, OPM is making minor wording and ordering 
  2888  changes to this provision. Section 351.605(c) provides that any 
  2889  competing employee released under this provision must be provided a 
  2890  specific written notice in accordance with Sec.  351.801, Notice 
  2891  period. The notice must include the following: the action being taken 
  2892  and its effective date; the competitive area being abolished; a link to 
  2893  5 CFR part 351 and access to the agency's records pertinent to the RIF 
  2894  being run to abolish the competitive area; information on reemployment 
  2895  rights; the employee's appeal rights; and a statement that, because all 
  2896  positions in the competitive area are being abolished pursuant to 5 CFR 
  2897  351.605, the employee was not ranked relative to other competing 
  2898  employees in the reduction in force. The notice is not required to 
  2899  include the information described in Sec.  351.802(a)(2) or (a)(4).
  2900      Section 351.605(d), Retention register not required, explains that 
  2901  an agency is not required to rank competing employees in the abolished 
  2902  competitive area, and must not apply the assignment right provisions in 
  2903  subpart G, because
  2904  
  2905  [[Page 49203]]
  2906  
  2907  no positions in the competitive area will remain.
  2908      Commenter 0683 suggested that OPM review and approve any 
  2909  competitive area abolishment due to the potential that agencies could 
  2910  use this provision alongside the new competitive area definition to 
  2911  evade the need to build a retention register and provide assignment 
  2912  rights. OPM believes that these concerns are adequately addressed by 
  2913  the requirement in Sec.  351.402(c) that OPM approve new or 
  2914  substantially modified competitive areas that have been in effect less 
  2915  than 90 days prior to the issuance of RIF notices; the requirement in 
  2916  Sec.  351.204 that agencies must administer and apply the regulations 
  2917  consistent with all applicable laws, including the Merit System 
  2918  Principles in 5 U.S.C. 2301(b); the requirement that the competitive 
  2919  area be disclosed to the employee in the RIF notice; and the 
  2920  availability of RIF appeal rights in Subpart I of 5 CFR part 351.
  2921      Commenter 0683 also asked that OPM clarify that the abolishment of 
  2922  a competitive area under Section 351.605 does not diminish or supersede 
  2923  the statutory placement rights of career SES members under 5 U.S.C. 
  2924  3594-3595. OPM confirms that these revisions are not intended to 
  2925  diminish or supersede career SES placement rights in a RIF. However, 
  2926  OPM believes that 5 CFR 359.602(b) is clear enough on this point that 
  2927  no change to the regulatory text in 5 CFR part 351 is required.
  2928  3. USERRA Rights
  2929      In the proposed rule, OPM proposed to modify Sec.  351.606(a), 
  2930  which addresses mandatory RIF exceptions for employees who have been 
  2931  restored or reemployed following uniformed service and who remain 
  2932  entitled to post-reemployment retention protection under Sec.  
  2933  353.209(b) for either 6 months or 1 year. These retention rights are 
  2934  provided under USERRA.
  2935      Commenter 0686, a Federal agency, requested that OPM clarify the 
  2936  proposed modifications to Sec.  351.606, and particularly its 
  2937  interaction with Sec.  351.605, which revises the procedures to be 
  2938  followed when a competitive area is abolished. Several other commenters 
  2939  (0076, 0121, 0455, 0550, 0597) argued that the proposed rule could be 
  2940  read as undermining USERRA rights, including where an employee 
  2941  performing uniformed service or recently reemployed after uniformed 
  2942  service lacks recent civilian performance ratings.
  2943      OPM agrees that clarification is appropriate. Accordingly, OPM in 
  2944  this final rule is making explicit how USERRA restoration and retention 
  2945  protections operate when an employee is affected by a RIF.
  2946      First, OPM is adding a definition of ``Restoration protected 
  2947  employee'' in Sec.  351.203. For purposes of part 351, a restoration 
  2948  protected employee is a competing employee who has been restored or 
  2949  reemployed following uniformed service and who, as of the date the 
  2950  employee receives a specific reduction in force notice, remains within 
  2951  the 6-month or 1-year post-reemployment protection period described in 
  2952  Sec.  353.209(b). Those protection periods implement 38 U.S.C. 4316(c), 
  2953  which provides that a person reemployed under USERRA may not be 
  2954  discharged from employment, except for cause, for 1 year after 
  2955  reemployment if the period of uniformed service was more than 180 days, 
  2956  or for 180 days after reemployment if the period of service was more 
  2957  than 30 days but less than 181 days.
  2958      Second, OPM is revising Sec.  351.606 to clarify that agencies must 
  2959  apply USERRA retention protections and restoration rights as a 
  2960  mandatory exception to the ordinary RIF order of release. The agency 
  2961  must first determine the employee's ordinary retention standing under 
  2962  subpart E. The agency must then apply the mandatory exception in Sec.  
  2963  351.606(a). During the applicable 6-month or 1-year protection period, 
  2964  the agency may not release a restoration protected employee from the 
  2965  competitive level if another competing employee may be released 
  2966  instead.
  2967      Third, OPM is clarifying how the mandatory exception applies when 
  2968  an agency abolishes all positions in a competitive area under Sec.  
  2969  351.605. When an entire competitive area is abolished pursuant to Sec.  
  2970  351.605, the agency may not separate the restoration protected employee 
  2971  by RIF during the applicable 6-month or 1-year protection period. 
  2972  Instead, the employee must be assigned by the agency to a different 
  2973  position of like seniority, status, and pay for which the employee is 
  2974  qualified, consistent with 5 CFR part 353.
  2975      Fourth, OPM is revising Sec.  353.209(a) to conform part 353 to 
  2976  these part 351 clarifications. Section 353.209(a) already provides that 
  2977  an employee performing duty with the uniformed services may not be 
  2978  demoted or separated, other than military separation, except for cause; 
  2979  that RIF is not ``for cause'' under that subpart; that the employee is 
  2980  not a competing employee under part 351; and that, if the employee's 
  2981  position is abolished during the absence, the agency must reassign the 
  2982  employee to another position of like status and pay. OPM is clarifying 
  2983  that this reassignment obligation applies when the employee's position 
  2984  is abolished in a RIF, including when all positions in the employee's 
  2985  competitive area are abolished under Sec.  351.605.
  2986      Fifth, OPM is clarifying the relationship between part 351, part 
  2987  353, and 38 U.S.C. 4314 when the employing agency can no longer place 
  2988  the employee. If the employee's function has been transferred to 
  2989  another agency, the employee's rights are governed by the transfer and 
  2990  restoration provisions in 5 CFR part 353. If the employing agency no 
  2991  longer exists and its functions have not been transferred, or if it is 
  2992  impossible or unreasonable for the agency to reassign the restoration 
  2993  protected employee, OPM will offer placement assistance elsewhere in 
  2994  the executive branch to the employee pursuant to 5 CFR 353.110.
  2995      These revisions also address concerns that employees performing 
  2996  uniformed service, or recently returned from uniformed service, may 
  2997  lack recent civilian ratings of record. This rule's missing-rating 
  2998  provisions continue to address how ordinary performance credit is 
  2999  calculated for competing employees who do not have three ratings of 
  3000  record, including use of the modal rating for employees with no ratings 
  3001  during the relevant four-year period and proxy rules for employees with 
  3002  one or two ratings. But for a restoration-protected employee within the 
  3003  6-month or 1-year post-reemployment protection period, the mandatory 
  3004  exception in Sec.  351.606(a) operates independently of the employee's 
  3005  ordinary retention standing. Thus, the employee is not penalized for 
  3006  lacking recent civilian ratings during the protected period; the agency 
  3007  must honor the USERRA retention protection before releasing the 
  3008  employee by RIF.
  3009      In addition, this rule preserves credit for uniformed service in 
  3010  calculating length of service for RIF purposes. Section 351.505(b)(1) 
  3011  provides that all active duty in a uniformed service, as defined in 5 
  3012  U.S.C. 2101(3), is creditable for purposes of part 351, except as 
  3013  otherwise provided in that section. The service computation date 
  3014  includes all actual creditable service under Sec.  351.505(a) and (b).
  3015  4. Exceptions
  3016      OPM is modifying and clarifying current Sec.  351.607, relabeling 
  3017  this section as Discretionary continuing exceptions to harmonize this 
  3018  section with other provisions in this chapter for which agency use is 
  3019  optional. OPM is also modifying and clarifying Sec.  351.608, renaming 
  3020  this section Discretionary
  3021  
  3022  [[Page 49204]]
  3023  
  3024  temporary exceptions. OPM is also creating new flexibilities for an 
  3025  agency to retain an employee past the effective date of a RIF due to a 
  3026  government obligation. Section 351.608(c) now includes additional 
  3027  examples of situations in which the exception may be used, such as when 
  3028  an employee, or spouse of an employee, is pregnant on the effective 
  3029  date of a RIF or an employee has not used all available paid parental 
  3030  leave to care for a recently born child or a child recently placed with 
  3031  the employee for adoption purposes.
  3032      Paragraph (d) of Sec.  351.608 expands the existing exception to 
  3033  allow employees with medical conditions or other circumstances that 
  3034  would qualify for use of sick leave to use other appropriate leave 
  3035  (paid or unpaid) or other paid time off in addition to sick leave, 
  3036  subject to a 90-day cap and provided that the leave is used 
  3037  continuously. Section 351.608(e) labels this provision ``annual leave'' 
  3038  to make clear the type of leave appropriate for an exception under this 
  3039  paragraph, which has been expanded to include not only employees 
  3040  covered by a Federal leave system under an authority other than 5 
  3041  U.S.C. chapter 63 but also employees covered by a retirement law not 
  3042  referenced in Sec.  351.606(b) or a health benefits law other than 5 
  3043  U.S.C. chapter 89. A new Sec.  351.608(f) establishes a temporary 
  3044  exception for military spouses as defined in Sec.  351.203. An agency 
  3045  may retain an eligible military spouse for up to 90 days beyond the 
  3046  effective date of a RIF. OPM did not receive significant adverse 
  3047  comment regarding its proposed changes to sections 351.607 and 351.608 
  3048  and is finalizing them.
  3049  
  3050  F. Part 351, Subpart G: Assignment Rights

Q13 candidates here:
- Lines 2838-2842: "OPM is modifying Sec. 351.602 to remove the prohibition on retaining an employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment in a competitive level while releasing a competing employee from that level." But final Sec. 351.602 text retains "An agency may not release a competing employee from a competitive level while retaining in that level an employee with: (a) A specifically limited temporary or term promotion; or (b) ...". Wait, this says "specifically limited temporary or term promotion", not appointment. Preamble says "temporary appointment" — that's a misstatement! Reg text prohibits retaining an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion, not appointment. Great Q13 item: preamble at 49202 says removing prohibition on retaining employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment; regulatory text at 49223 retains prohibition on retaining employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion. Another passage maybe states correctly? Search for "351.602" and "promotion". Later? Let's grep.
- Lines 2864-2872: "revised section explains that ... agency is not required to release competing employees in order of retention standing." Text 351.605(b). consistent.
- Lines 2888-2899: notice content list. Text 351.605(c) includes (a)(1),(a)(3),(a)(5),(a)(6),(b), identify competitive area, statement. Preamble says includes "action being taken and its effective date" (a)(1)? "competitive area being abolished" yes; "link to 5 CFR part 351 and access to records" (a)(3); "information on reemployment rights" (a)(5); "employee's appeal rights" (a)(6); statement. consistent.
- Lines 2913-2915: "requirement in Sec. 351.402(c) that OPM approve new or substantially modified competitive areas that have been in effect less than 90 days prior to issuance of RIF notices." Text 351.402(c): "If an agency establishes or materially modifies a competitive area within 90 days before issuing specific RIF notices..." Preamble "have been in effect less than 90 days" vs text "establishes ... within 90 days before". Similar but different trigger. Could be Q13 item. Another passage lines 2235-2240 similar. Hmm.
- Lines 2929-2932: "proposed to modify Sec. 351.606(a), which addresses mandatory RIF exceptions for employees who have been restored or reemployed following uniformed service and who remain entitled to post-reemployment retention protection under Sec. 353.209(b) for either 6 months or 1 year." Text 351.606(a)(1) says "entitled under Sec. 353.209(b) to retention for, as applicable, 6 months or 1 year after restoration." consistent.
- Lines 2946-2957: "Restoration protected employee ... as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice, remains within the 6-month or 1-year post-reemployment protection period described in Sec. 353.209(b). Those protection periods implement 38 U.S.C. 4316(c), which provides ... 1 year after reemployment if period of uniformed service was more than 180 days, or for 180 days after reemployment if period ... more than 30 days but less than 181 days." Text 351.203 definition: "remains entitled under Sec. 353.209(b) ... to retention for six (6) months or one (1) year after restoration." Good. Note 6 months vs 180 days; not exactly but okay.
- Lines 2967-2974: "When an entire competitive area is abolished ... the agency may not separate the restoration protected employee by RIF during the applicable 6-month or 1-year protection period. Instead, the employee must be assigned by the agency to a different position of like seniority, status, and pay for which the employee is qualified, consistent with 5 CFR part 353." Text 351.606(a)(3) says "must instead reassign the employee, as necessary, to another position of like seniority, status, and pay for which the employee is qualified, consistent with part 353". consistent.
- Lines 3032-3036: "Paragraph (d) of Sec. 351.608 expands the existing exception to allow employees with medical conditions ... to use other appropriate leave ... subject to a 90-day cap..." Text 351.608(d)(4) 90 days. consistent.
- Lines 3043-3046: "A new Sec. 351.608(f) establishes a temporary exception for military spouses ... up to 90 days." Text 351.608(f) says agency may establish maximum number of days, up to 90. consistent.

Need Subpart G/H preamble 3050-3198 for Q6(e) and Q13.

  3050  F. Part 351, Subpart G: Assignment Rights
  3051  
  3052      OPM is revising Sec.  351.701(a) to replace tenure groups I and II 
  3053  with the competitive service tenure group in conformance with other 
  3054  changes in this rulemaking.
  3055      OPM is consolidating Sec.  351.701(b) and (c), simplifying the 
  3056  method of applying assignment rights. Based on the new method of 
  3057  defining tenure groups and assigning retention standing based on 
  3058  performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference, with tenure 
  3059  subgroup and length of service as tiebreakers, subgroups will no longer 
  3060  play a predominant role in determining retention standing, and thus 
  3061  there is no longer a need for the separate concepts of an employee 
  3062  ``bumping'' another employee in a lower subgroup, and ``retreating'' to 
  3063  the position of a lower-ranked employee in the same subgroup. Instead, 
  3064  a released employee will have assignment rights to a position held by 
  3065  another employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure 
  3066  group, who is not more than three grades below the position from which 
  3067  the employee was released, and for which the released employee is 
  3068  qualified, pursuant to the criteria set forth in Sec.  351.702 and 
  3069  Sec.  351.703. This reform will significantly simplify the process of 
  3070  applying assignment rights in a RIF, eliminating the need for 
  3071  successive rounds of bumping and retreating between and within 
  3072  different subgroups.
  3073      OPM is eliminating Sec.  351.701(d). With the new method of 
  3074  calculating retention standing implemented in this rulemaking, which 
  3075  emphasizes performance over tenure and length of service, OPM believes 
  3076  that this restriction on employees with a current annual performance 
  3077  rating of record of Level 2 from obtaining assignment to positions held 
  3078  by employees with a higher performance rating is no longer necessary. 
  3079  OPM did not receive significant adverse comment on the removal of this 
  3080  provision.
  3081      OPM is modifying Sec.  351.702(a)(4), pertaining to qualifications 
  3082  for assignment to a new position, to include language clarifying that 
  3083  in determining qualifications for reassignment an agency must use an 
  3084  assessment that allows for demonstration of job-related skills, 
  3085  abilities, knowledge, and competencies; is based on a job analysis; and 
  3086  does not rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination. 
  3087  Commenter 0687 supported this change, expressing ``appreciat[ion] that 
  3088  OPM has added a mechanism for agencies to utilize assessments to 
  3089  determine qualification for those assignments that is skills-based and 
  3090  consistent with merit principles in selection.''
  3091      On the other hand, Commenter 0685 expressed concern that the use of 
  3092  assessments would ``inject subjectivity into what has traditionally 
  3093  been a more mechanical qualification determination.'' OPM disagrees. 
  3094  The current rule provides that an employee is qualified for a position 
  3095  if the employee ``[h]as the capacity, adaptability, and special skills 
  3096  needed to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position without 
  3097  undue interruption,'' but provides no other guidance for making this 
  3098  determination, other than that an agency may consider ``recency of 
  3099  experience, when appropriate.'' OPM believes that the use of a 
  3100  validated assessment that allows for demonstration of job-related 
  3101  skills, abilities, knowledge, and competencies, such as a structured 
  3102  interview, structured resume review, or a work-related exercise, will 
  3103  reduce the subjectivity of making a qualifications determination, 
  3104  requiring that an employee demonstrate their job-related skills in a 
  3105  measured, objective fashion. In so doing, OPM is aligning qualification 
  3106  determinations for assignment in a RIF with otherwise-applicable merit-
  3107  based hiring practices required under E.O. 13932, E.O. 14171, the 
  3108  Chance to Compete Act of 2024 (Pub. L. 118-188), and the Merit Hiring 
  3109  Plan.\17\
  3110  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  3111  
  3112      \17\ Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy & OPM, Merit

  3116      However, OPM recognizes that, in some circumstances, requiring a 
  3117  new assessment may be unnecessary where official records already show

  3120  providing that an agency is not required to administer an assessment

  3124  duties, occupational series, qualification requirements, and conditions 
  3125  of employment, and received a rating of record of Level 3, Fully 
  3126  Successful, or higher, or the equivalent, for performance of those 
  3127  duties. This provision is intended to reduce unnecessary assessments 
  3128  while preserving the requirement that assignment rights be based on the 
  3129  employee's ability to perform the work.
  3130      OPM is modifying current Sec.  351.705 Administrative assignment to 
  3131  eliminate references to optional agency flexibilities to allow

  3133  higher standing in the same subgroup under certain circumstances. With

Q13 candidates:
- Lines 3055-3066: "OPM is consolidating Sec. 351.701(b) and (c), simplifying the method of applying assignment rights... a released employee will have assignment rights to a position held by another employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group, who is not more than three grades below the position from which the employee was released..." But text 351.701(b)(2) provides exception for 30% disabled up to five grades. Preamble here omits the five-grade exception. Later? Executive summary item 12 mentions five grades. Could be Q13 item: preamble at 49204 says assignment rights "not more than three grades below" without mentioning five-grade exception for 30%+ disabled; text 351.701(b)(2) says three grades, except five grades for preference eligible with 30%+ disability. Another passage (executive summary at 49178) states correctly. Strong.
- Lines 3073-3078: "OPM is eliminating Sec. 351.701(d). ... this restriction on employees with a current annual performance rating of record of Level 2 from obtaining assignment to positions held by employees with a higher performance rating is no longer necessary." But final 351.701(a) still requires current annual rating of Level 2 or higher to have assignment rights. Wait—the "restriction" being eliminated is 351.701(d), which likely said employees rated Level 2 could not displace employees with higher performance ratings. Preamble says eliminating that restriction. Text 351.701(a) retains requirement of Level 2 or higher. Consistent: Level 2 employees can get assignment rights, but not restricted from displacing higher-rated employees. Fine. But is there a Q13 issue: preamble says "employees with a current annual performance rating of record of Level 2" while text 351.701(a) says "minimally satisfactory (Level 2) or equivalent, or higher". Fine.
- Lines 3116-3129: exception 5-year period; text matches.
- Lines 3130-3135: "modifying current Sec. 351.705 Administrative assignment to eliminate references to optional agency flexibilities to allow employees with lower retention standing to displace an employee with higher standing in the same subgroup under certain circumstances." Final 351.705(a) says agency may adopt provisions for excepted service assignment rights; no elimination apparent because only (a) revised. Maybe other paragraphs of 351.705 not printed remain? Could be. Not a Q13 item.
- Lines 3145-3168: 351.802(a) intro. Text matches.
- Lines 3169-3175: proposed to substitute "veterans' status" for "subgroup"; final "veterans' preference subgroup." Text 351.802(a)(2) says "veterans' preference subgroup." consistent. But note preamble says "add references to notifying employees of their tenure group and subgroup." Text says "tenure group and subgroup" yes.
- Lines 3176-3194: Sec. 351.805(b) amendment "conform that provision to proposed Sec. 351.507." But 351.507 was proposed and final; wording "proposed Sec. 351.507" maybe inaccurate—Sec. 351.507 is final. Not a substantive difference.

Also Q13 might involve the executive summary item 12 vs text: "generally within three grades below ... or five grades for certain 30-percent-or-more disabled veterans" correct. Item 13: exception "held the same or substantially similar position within five years of the RIF and achieved a rating of Level 3 ... for performing the duties of the position" — text says "during the 5-year period ending on the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice" and "same position, or a position at the same grade or pay level with substantially the same duties, occupational series, qualification requirements, and conditions of employment" and rating Level 3 or higher. Executive summary says "same or substantially similar position" but text includes same grade/pay level with substantially same duties, etc. Slight difference in category—could be Q13 item. But "for example a different category of employee" - yes.

Also executive summary item 2 says "Employees serving initial probationary periods, trial periods, temporary or time-limited appointments of one year or less, and Schedule C and Schedule G employees are not 'competing employees'..." Text (d)(1)(i) excepted temporary/time-limited ≤1 year; (d)(2)(iii) competitive temporary ≤1 year (not time-limited). So executive summary says "temporary or time-limited appointments of one year or less" generally, but text omits competitive time-limited. Another passage lines 1656-1662 correct. Good Q13 item (executive summary at 49178 vs text at 49218).

Also executive summary item 12: "assignment rights to a qualifying position held by another employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group, generally within three grades below the released employee's position, or five grades for certain 30-percent-or-more disabled veterans." Text matches.

Executive summary item 4: "three most recent ratings of record from the relevant four-year period, assigning 7 points for Level 5, 5 points for Level 4, 3 points for Level 3, and 0 points for Level 1 or Level 2 ratings, with special rules for missing ratings and differing appraisal patterns." Text matches.

Executive summary item 5: "Preference eligibles with a compensable service-connected disability of 30 percent or more receive 5 additional points; other preference eligibles receive 3 additional points; non-preference eligibles receive no additional points." Text matches.

Executive summary item 10: "agencies may define certain geographic locations as separate competitive areas, while employees working at approved alternate locations remain assigned to their official organizational unit for competitive area purposes." Text 351.402(b)(2),(3) matches.

Executive summary item 11: "When abolishing all positions in a competitive area within 180 days, agencies may release employees without ranking them on a retention register or applying assignment rights, and with a simplified notice." Text matches.

Executive summary item 16: "fixes retention standing as of the date the employee receives a specific RIF notice (rather than the date the RIF is executed)" — text 351.507(a) matches.

Potential Q13 mismatches:
1. Erosion of duties: preamble says 351.201(a)(2), 180 days; text 351.202(c)(3), adverse effect/period until completion. Another passage correct.
2. Competitive service temporary/time-limited appointments: executive summary/preamble says temporary or time-limited; text only temporary under subpart D; another passage correct.
3. Preference eligible "veterans" vs "employees": preamble 49197 says "veteran"; text 351.504(a) says employee; another passage correct (2481-2483).
4. Assignment rights three grades: preamble 49204 omits five-grade exception; text 351.701(b)(2) includes; another passage (exec summary) correct.
5. 351.602 "temporary appointment" vs "temporary or term promotion": preamble 49202 says appointment; text says promotion; need see if another passage correct. Search.
6. "as of date of RIF notice" vs "receives specific RIF notice" in tenure group discussion; text uses receives; another passage correct.
7. Competitive service tenure subgroup II "temporary or term appointment" vs text "temporary appointment" — perhaps same as #2.
8. 351.506(c) "consistent with changes in Sec. 351.505" maybe should be 351.503/504; minor.
9. 351.402(c) "in effect less than 90 days" vs text "establishes or materially modifies within 90 days before" — maybe.
10. 351.608(d) "90-day cap" text yes.
11. 351.606 restoration: preamble says "6-month or 1-year" but 38 U.S.C. 4316(c) provides 1 year if more than 180 days, 180 days if more than 30 but less than 181; text 351.203 says six months or one year. consistent.
12. Executive summary item 13: "same or substantially similar position within five years of the RIF" vs text "during the 5-year period ending on the date the employee receives a specific RIF notice" and "same position, or a position at same grade or pay level with substantially the same duties..." Could be a category difference. Another passage lines 3116-3129 states text accurately. Good Q13 item.

Let's search 351.602 in main rule preamble.

content.text:
Great: Q13 item #5 confirmed: preamble 49202 says "temporary appointment" while text 49223 says "temporary or term promotion." But wait—does another passage state correctly? Maybe not. Preamble says "remove prohibition on retaining employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment" — this is wrong twice: (1) appointment vs promotion; (2) "remove the prohibition" vs text still prohibits. Actually final 351.602 prohibits retaining an employee with "a specifically limited temporary or term promotion." The preamble says "remove the prohibition on retaining an employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment." So it misstates what the rule does: it says removing prohibition, but text retains prohibition for temporary or term promotion. Wait, maybe the old rule's 351.602 said "temporary or term promotion" and the new rule removes "temporary appointment" (not promotion)? Let's recall old 351.602: "An agency may not release a competing employee from a competitive level while retaining in that level an employee with: (a) A specifically limited temporary or term promotion; or (b) a written decision..." So current rule already prohibited temporary or term promotion. The final rule text retains it. Preamble says modifying 351.602 to remove prohibition on retaining employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment—maybe OPM meant "promotion" but wrote "appointment." No other passage. Strong Q13 item.

Also line 3136-3141: "OPM is retaining, and renumbering, current Sec. 351.705(c)" but final instruction revises 351.705(a), not (c)! The final 351.705(a) text is the excepted-service discretionary assignment provision that preamble says is current 351.705(c) renumbered. Final text shows "Sec. 351.705 Administrative assignment. (a) An agency may..." So it moves current (c) to (a). Preamble says "retaining, and renumbering, current Sec. 351.705(c)" which is consistent enough (renumbering to (a)). Fine.

Now Q9: We need identify which steps comply. Let's map each with provisions. But first need Q9 step 1 competitive area: 351.402(b)(1): organizational unit must be designated/approved by head of agency or designee; cannot be delegated below headquarters level. The scenario: Tulsa Field Office designated as separate competitive area Aug 17, 2026; agency head's designee approved; nothing sent to OPM. Notice Oct 13, 2026. Under 351.402(c): if agency establishes or materially modifies a competitive area within 90 days before issuing specific RIF notices, it shall submit description + written statement to OPM for approval in advance of RIF. Aug 17 to Oct 13 = 57 days < 90, so must submit to OPM. Nothing sent -> noncompliant. Also the designation was by agency head's designee; allowed (can't delegate below HQ level, but designee okay). The field office is on official org chart and distinguished; fine. So step 1 noncompliant solely for failure to submit to OPM.

Step 2: Ms. Novak, career-conditional hired March 2026, still serving initial probationary period, kept while career employee in same level released. Under 351.202(d)(2)(ii), career-conditional employee serving initial probationary period is not a competing employee; agency may retain such employee while releasing a competing employee (351.202(d)(3)). So in order. Note: Q assumptions say "A 'career' employee has completed initial probationary period" and Novak is career-conditional still probationary. Good.

Step 3: Ms. Ortiz career tenure, promoted to first supervisory position June 2026, serving supervisory probationary period. Left off register because "on probation." Under 351.203 "Initial probationary period" excludes probationary period applicable on initial appointment to supervisory/managerial position. So she is not serving an initial probationary period; 351.202(d) does not exclude her. She must be on register and ranked. Preamble lines 1610-1617 says career employee only on supervisory probation is included in RIF in supervisory position. So noncompliant. What rules require: include her in competitive service tenure subgroup I (career), rank on register; supervisory probation does not exclude.

Step 4: cutoff date 30 days before notices issued. Notice Oct 13; cutoff = Sept 13, 2026. A rating of record signed, issued, put on record Oct 2, 2026 was used for Mr. Pruitt "because it raised his score. No other employee's later rating was used." Wait: cutoff date Sept 13; rating Oct 2 is after cutoff. Under 351.503(c)(2): when cutoff date used, performance credit based on three most recent ratings received during 4-year period prior to cutoff date. A rating received after cutoff cannot be used. Also 351.503(c)(3) requires on record; but after cutoff. So using Oct 2 rating is noncompliant. "No other employee's later rating was used" doesn't cure; must be uniformly applied (351.503(c)(4)). So noncompliant. Rules require not use it; recalculate Pruitt without it. Unless "cutoff date" was 30 days before notices = Sept 13; Oct 2 > Sept 13. Yes.

Step 5: Ms. Quist two ratings 5 and 4; missing scored as presumed Level 3, giving 7+5+3=15. Under 351.503(f)(2), proxy = (7+5)/2 = 6; performance credit = 7+5+6 = 18, not 15. Noncompliant. Note Level 3 = 3, but proxy is numeric average 6 (not a summary level). So wrong.

Step 6: Agency adds 2 points to performance credit of every employee who received QSI in last 4 years. Under 351.503(d)(1), additional points for performance are permitted only in "single rating pattern" where highest summary level is level 3 (pass/fail) and only for level 3 employees with demonstrated exceptional performance and agency action; not across-the-board for QSI recipients in a five-level pattern. Also 351.503(e) multiple rating patterns for transmuting; not this. The scenario says all rated under one five-level pattern (Q9 intro). So additional 2 points for QSI is not authorized. Noncompliant. Could an agency use 351.503(d) or (e)? No—those are limited. Also 351.503(c)(4) uniformity; but substantive authority lacking. Noncompliant.

Step 7: Two employees at bottom of one register same performance credit with veterans points, same tenure subgroup, same SCD. Office director chose which to release. Under 351.601(c), agency may select any tied employee for release. So in order. "Office director" presumably agency official; no issue.

Step 8: Agency released competing employee while retaining Mr. Reyes, who is in level on a temporary promotion that ends March 2027. Under 351.602(a), agency may not release competing employee from competitive level while retaining employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion. So noncompliant. Rules require not retain Reyes in that level; either include/rank him? Actually prohibition means cannot release while retaining him. Need terminate promotion or release? The provision says agency may not release a competing employee while retaining in that level an employee with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion. So the agency must not retain Reyes in the level while releasing others; must either return him to his permanent position (if outside level) or include him? The rule doesn't prescribe; but action noncompliant.

Step 9: Mr. Silva released from competitive level, offered lower-grade position without any assessment because he held same position until 2023 and received Level 4 rating in it in 2022. Under 351.702(a)(4)(v), agency not required to administer assessment if during 5-year period ending on date employee receives specific RIF notice, employee occupied same position or same grade/pay level with substantially same duties, occupational series, qualification requirements, conditions, and received rating Level 3+ for performance of those duties. Silva held same position until 2023 (within 5 years of Oct 13, 2026), Level 4 in 2022. So exception applies; in order. Note "offered a position at a lower grade" — must also be within assignment rights grade limit; not stated, but question step focuses on assessment. Could be in order if within grade limit and held by lower-standing employee. Assume yes? The step says "offered a position at a lower grade without any assessment... because he had held that same position until 2023 and received a Level 4 rating of record in it in 2022." Likely testing 351.702(a)(4)(v). In order.

Step 10: Qualification for assignment decided from an online self-rating questionnaire that is scored automatically. Under 351.702(a)(4)(iii), assessment must "[d]oes not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment." An online self-rating questionnaire scored automatically is exactly prohibited. Noncompliant. Must use assessment that allows demonstration of job-related skills, based on job analysis, not solely/principally automated self-assessment; examples structured interviews, work exercise, etc.

Step 11: Keep Ms. Tran 60 days after Dec 14 under undue interruption exception (351.608(b) allows not more than 90 days), and then further 60 days under general temporary exception for other reasons (351.608(g) allows up to 90 days). But 351.608(a)(3): each exception stands alone and may not be sequenced or stacked in combination with another exception. So stacking 60 + 60 is noncompliant. Also first 60 under (b) okay (≤90); second 60 under (g) okay individually (≤90), but stacking violates (a)(3). The agency may apply exception providing longest period of retention (90 days), not combine. So noncompliant.

Step 12: Each notice said may appeal to MSPB within 30 days after it takes effect. Under new rules (notices Oct 13, 2026, after Sept 2), appeals go to OPM, not MSPB; 351.802(a)(6) requires notice of right to appeal to OPM, time limit under 351.902(b), and electronic filing system. So noncompliant. Also time limit: 30 calendar days from effective date, not "within 30 days after it takes effect" (roughly same but forum wrong). Must state OPM appeal rights and filing info.

Step 1 detail: Also note designation approved by agency head's designee—is that allowed? Text: "must be designated/approved by the head of the agency, or designee, and the designation or approval cannot be delegated to an official below the agency's headquarters level." If designee at HQ level, fine. The scenario says agency head's designee approved; likely okay. Nothing sent to OPM is the violation because established within 90 days before notices (Aug 17 to Oct 13 = 57 days). Actually text: "If an agency establishes or materially modifies a competitive area within 90 days before issuing specific reduction in force notices for that competitive area, the agency shall submit a description ... to OPM for approval in advance of the reduction in force." Yes.

Also step 1: The Tulsa Field Office was "first designated it as a separate competitive area on August 17, 2026." Was it previously part of a larger competitive area? If so, establishing new competitive area within 90 days triggers. Yes.

Step 4 cutoff: 30 days before Oct 13 = Sept 13, 2026. Is Sept 13 a Sunday; but cutoff date is specified number of days; no adjustment rule. Fine. Rating Oct 2 after cutoff. Could the agency's policy set cutoff date 30 days before notice issuance; yes under 351.503(c)(2). But using later rating violates. Also "no other employee's later rating was used" — disparate treatment violates 351.503(c)(4) uniformity. Good.

Step 5: Proxy calculation with 5 and 4: (7+5)/2 = 6; total 18. Note if rating values are Level 5=7, Level 4=5. Yes.

Step 8: Could Reyes be a "competing employee" on temporary promotion? 351.602 prohibits retaining employee with specifically limited temporary or term promotion. Yes.

Step 9: 351.702(a)(4)(v) exception applies if "during the 5-year period ending on the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice, the employee occupied the same position, or a position at the same grade or pay level with substantially the same duties, occupational series, qualification requirements, and conditions of employment, and received a rating of record of Level 3, Fully Successful, or higher, or equivalent, for performance of those duties." He held same position until 2023; notice Oct 13, 2026; 2023 is within 5 years; Level 4 in 2022 for that position. In order. But wait, "until 2023" could be before Oct 13, 2021? No, 2023 is within 5 years. Good.

Step 11: First 60 days "under the exception for avoiding undue interruption" = 351.608(b) "not more than 90 days"; 60 okay. Further 60 under "general temporary exception for other reasons" = 351.608(g) "up to 90 days"; 60 okay. But stacking prohibited by (a)(3). Also note if the agency determines it can approve more than one exception, may apply exception that provides longest period; 90 days max. So total retention cannot exceed 90 days under one exception, not 120. Noncompliant.

Step 12: Under 351.802(a)(6) as revised by 2026-15666, notice must include right to appeal to OPM, time limit under 351.902(b), electronic filing system. Also 351.901(c)(4) no judicial review; not relevant. Noncompliant.

Are any other steps noncompliant? Step 2: Novak career-conditional serving initial probationary period; agency kept her while releasing career employee—yes allowed. But could there be issue that she was "hired March 2026" and career-conditional—initial probationary period typically 1 year; still serving. Yes. 351.202(d)(3) allows retain. Good.

Step 3: Ortiz career tenure, first supervisory position June 2026, supervisory probationary. Because "initial probationary period" definition excludes supervisory probation; she is not excluded. Must be ranked. Noncompliant. Also if she is in a different competitive level due to supervisory position? Assume same level? The scenario says "left off the retention register for her competitive level"; so yes.

Step 6: Could 351.503(d) permit additional points for QSI recipients? Only for employees covered under a summary level appraisal system in which the highest summary level is a level 3 (pattern A pass/fail or pattern D). The scenario says all rated under one five-level pattern, so no. Also "quality step increase" is one of the listed performance actions, but only in the single rating pattern context. Noncompliant.

Step 4: If the agency sets cutoff 30 days before notices, all employees' ratings after cutoff excluded. The Oct 2 rating was before notice Oct 13 but after cutoff Sept 13. Not usable. Good.

Step 9: What if "same position until 2023" but the position offered is at a lower grade; perhaps he held "that same position" meaning the lower-grade position. The exception applies to "the same position, or a position at the same grade or pay level with substantially the same duties..." If he held the exact same position, yes. Level 4 rating. In order.

Step 10: "online self-rating questionnaire that is scored automatically" may not "consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment." Yes.

Step 12: Is MSPB appeal possible for RIF action? Under 2026 rules, no; OPM. The notice must state right to appeal to OPM. Noncompliant.

Now Q2/Q12 arithmetic and Q4/Q5 etc. Need also Q6 details and Q7, Q8, Q10. We have enough.

But Q11 requires full comparison; we need more of proposed and final text maybe for 351.601-608 and 351.701-705, already read. Also 351.202-203. Good.

Need Q1(d) implementation section maybe read lines 3395-3418.
