content.text:
Q1(d) answer: DATES 91 FR 49178 and Implementation 91 FR 49207: based on date agency issues RIF notice. RIFs noticed before Sept 2, 2026 under old rules; notices on/after Sept 2 under amended rules. Also 351.507 notes retention standing as of receipt, but implementation based on issuance date. Good.

Now Q5(a) old rules details. Need old performance credit values: Level 5 = 20 years, Level 4 = 16, Level 3 = 12 (lines 1092-1094). Need maybe cite FR page 49186. Also old ranking: tenure group then veterans' preference subgroup AD/A/B then years of service as augmented by performance credit, earliest service date (lines 2496-2501, FR 49198). Also note old rules performance credits averaged, rounded, expressed as additional years of service (lines 1088-1094). For Lee (3,3,3) average 12 years. Park (5,5,5) average 20 years. Both Group I, subgroup B. Adjusted SCD Lee 1998-12 = 1986; Park 2019-20 = 1999. Lee ahead. Under new rules: Lee 9, Park 21; Park ahead. Good.

Q2(c): old rules Bianchi AD vs Abbott B; AD ahead regardless of performance/SCD. Cite lines 2496-2501 (91 FR 49198): "ranked first by tenure group I, II, III; then within each tenure group by veterans' preference subgroup AD, A, B; and only then by years of service as augmented by performance credit". Also line 620-623: "a veteran in tenure group II is ranked below a non-veteran in tenure group I" and within group preference subgroups. Good.

Now Q3 details and Q12 maybe need 353.209(b) background: 38 U.S.C. 4316(c) periods; preamble lines 2946-2957 says 1 year if more than 180 days, 180 days if more than 30 but less than 181. Farouk 14 months >180 -> 1 year. So protected until July 13, 2027. Good. We can cite preamble at 91 FR 49203 and definition 351.203.

Wait: Q12 Farouk "away for 14 months of uniformed service and was restored to his position under 5 CFR part 353 on July 13, 2026." Under 38 U.S.C. 4316(c), if period of service more than 180 days, 1 year after reemployment. So retention protection through July 13, 2027. Notice Oct 5, 2026; within. Good.

But Q12(b): Which three employees released from GS-13 level? If Farouk protected, the agency may not release him if another competing employee may be released instead. There are 6 competing employees; 3 positions abolished; Quinn excluded retained. Need release three. The lowest three not protected: Brandt (13), Estrada (16), Dube (18). But wait, could the agency release Farouk anyway because "another competing employee may be released instead" yes there are enough others: Brandt, Estrada, Dube. So Farouk retained. Good.

But check whether Dube is actually lower than Estrada? Dube 18 > Estrada 16. Yes. Lowest are Farouk 9 (protected), Brandt 13, Estrada 16, Dube 18, Chen 18, Alvarez 19. Need 3 releases: Brandt, Estrada, Dube. But Dube ties Chen at 18; Chen subgroup I > Dube subgroup II, so Dube below Chen. Yes.

Now, assignment rights among released:
- Brandt (13, AD) could displace Ikeda (9, GS-9) [5-grade limit; compare: Ikeda 9 lower; also Hill 14 higher, Jones 15 higher, Gomez 17 higher].
- Estrada (16) could displace Hill (14) and Jones (15) and Ikeda (9) but grade limit 3 from GS-13: GS-12, GS-11, GS-10; GS-9 excluded. Least reduction: GS-11 Hill. But could Estrada displace Gomez (17)? No, Gomez higher (17 > 16).
- Dube (18) could displace Gomez (17), Hill (14), Jones (15), Ikeda (9). Grade limit 3: GS-12, GS-11, GS-10. Least reduction: GS-12 Gomez. Dube's subgroup II vs Gomez subgroup I doesn't matter because total 18 > 17. Good.

But do multiple released employees' assignment rights interact? Suppose Dube displaces Gomez (GS-12); Gomez then released from GS-12; but Gomez only qualified for his own position, so separated. Suppose Estrada displaces Hill; Hill separated. Brandt displaces Ikeda; Ikeda separated. That's consistent. But is it possible that Estrada, with 16, could displace Jones (15) at GS-10, and Brandt (13) could displace Ikeda; then Hill (14) remains. But agency must offer "least possible reduction in representative rate" — Estrada must be offered GS-11 Hill, not GS-10 Jones. Yes. What if Hill is already displaced by someone else? Only Estrada and Dube have rights; Dube chooses GS-12; so Hill available. Fine. Then Jones remains.

Could Dube, because subgroup II, be prohibited from displacing Gomez who is subgroup I? Text: "held by another employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group." Both are in competitive service tenure group. "Lower retention standing" determined by 351.501: performance credit augmented by veterans' pref first, then tenure subgroup. Dube 18 vs Gomez 17 -> Dube higher. Yes. So Dube can displace Gomez. Good.

What about released employees being "career-conditional" Dube vs career Gomez: same tenure group, different subgroups; assignment rights are within same tenure group, not subgroup. Good.

What about assignment rights of Brandt (AD 30%) to GS-9 Ikeda: 5 grades below GS-13 -> GS-8? Wait "not more than five grades (or appropriate grade intervals or equivalent) below." GS-13 down 5 grades = GS-8. GS-9 is 4 grades below, so within. Good.

Now Q12(d): "If every offer is accepted, who is separated from the agency in this RIF?" Dube displaces Gomez; Estrada displaces Hill; Brandt displaces Ikeda. Those three holders are released from their competitive levels. Do they have assignment rights? Each is qualified only for the position they hold, so no assignment rights to any other position. Thus separated. What about the released GS-13 employees? They accept offers and are assigned; not separated. What about Farouk, Alvarez, Chen, Quinn, Jones? Remain. So separations: Gomez, Hill, Ikeda. But wait: If Gomez is displaced by Dube, Gomez is a career employee with 17 points; could he have assignment rights to the GS-11/10/9 positions? He is qualified only for the position he holds (GS-12), so no. Yes.

However, there is a subtle issue: The GS-12 position held by Gomez is in its own competitive level (one position). If Dube displaces Gomez, is Gomez "released from his competitive level" and does he get assignment rights to lower positions? 351.701(a) applies to competitive service tenure group employee released from a competitive level. But Gomez is qualified only for his current position; assignment rights require qualification for offered position. None. So separated. Same Hill, Ikeda.

But wait—what about "bumping" into a position held by someone with lower retention standing in same tenure group; Gomez's own position is being taken by Dube. Could Gomez displace someone at lower grade? Not qualified. Good.

Now Q6: Need determine assignment rights. Let's carefully parse 351.701:
(a) "When a competitive service tenure group employee with a current annual performance rating of record of minimally satisfactory (Level 2) or equivalent, or higher, is released from a competitive level, an agency must offer assignment, rather than furlough or separation, in accordance with paragraph (b) ... to another competitive position that requires no reduction, or the least possible reduction, in representative rate. The employee must be qualified for the offered position. The offered position must be in the same competitive area and have the same type of work schedule ... as the position from which the employee is released."
(b) "a released employee shall be assigned to a position: (1) That is held by another employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group; and (2) That is not more than three grades (or appropriate grade intervals or equivalent) below the position from which the employee was released, except that for a preference eligible employee with a compensable service-connected disability of 30 percent or more the limit is five grades ... (The agency uses the grade progression of only the released employee's position of record to determine the applicable grades ...); and (3) For which the released employee is qualified..."
So positions:
1. GS-12 Ellis lower standing -> available. This requires least reduction in representative rate? Jordan GS-13; GS-12 is one grade lower. Yes.
2. GS-11 Frank lower -> available, but less favorable than GS-12; agency must offer GS-12 because "no reduction, or least possible reduction, in representative rate."
3. GS-10 Gale lower -> available within 3 grades, but less favorable.
4. GS-9 Hana lower -> not available (4 grades below; unless 30%+ disability -> 5 grades, then available but less favorable).
5. GS-12 Ito higher standing -> not available.
6. GS-12 part-time Kim lower -> not available due to different type of work schedule (position from which Jordan released is full-time; assumption full-time).
7. GS-12 Lund lower but different competitive area -> not available.
(a) So assignment rights to positions 1,2,3 (and perhaps 4 if 30%+), but must offer position 1 (GS-12 Ellis). Explain each.

(b) If Jordan is preference eligible with 30%+ disability: five-grade limit -> GS-9 also available; still must offer GS-12 Ellis as least reduction. Also note 351.701(b)(2) and (f) pay band not relevant. So answer: same mandatory offer; assignment rights extend to GS-9 Hana (if lower standing), but because agency must offer least possible reduction, offer remains GS-12 Ellis. If Ellis not available? But scenario says held by Ellis lower. Good.

(c) If Jordan's current annual rating is Level 1: 351.701(a) requires current annual performance rating of Level 2 or higher. Level 1 -> no assignment rights at all. So none of the positions; agency may separate/furlough. Note "current annual performance rating of record" and 351.703? fine.

(d) If Jordan and all seven holders are in excepted service: 351.701 applies to "competitive service tenure group employee"; 351.705(a) allows agency discretion to adopt provisions giving excepted service employees assignment rights to other positions under same appointing authority on same basis as 351.701. So no statutory/regulatory entitlement; only if agency has adopted such provisions. If not, no assignment right; agency discretion. Also a RIF in excepted service uses excepted service tenure group. The question asks "How does it change if Jordan and all seven position holders are in the excepted service?" Answer: no mandatory assignment rights; 351.705(a) permits agency discretion. If agency adopted provisions, same analysis could apply by analogy; but not required.

(e) Old HR handbook says Level 2 cannot take position held by someone with higher rating, distinguishes "bumping" from "retreating." What do 2026 documents say about each?
- Final rule eliminates Sec. 351.701(d): the restriction on employees with current annual rating of Level 2 from obtaining assignment to positions held by employees with a higher performance rating is no longer necessary (preamble 91 FR 49204, lines 3073-3078). Regulatory text 351.701(a) now allows Level 2 or higher; no separate restriction. So handbook statement is outdated: Level 2 employees can take positions held by employees with higher ratings if other requirements met.
- "Bumping" and "retreating" concepts replaced: preamble 91 FR 49204 (lines 3055-3072) says no longer need separate concepts of bumping in lower subgroup and retreating to position of lower-ranked employee in same subgroup; instead assignment rights to position held by another employee with lower retention standing in same tenure group. Also executive summary item 12 says replacing bump and retreat concepts. So handbook's distinction is obsolete. Need cite.

Now Q7(a) documents: 2026-15666, 2026-16456. Maybe also 2026-02576 proposed? The question says "Give every 2026 document that bears on the answer." Could include the proposed rule (which proposed prospective application) but a proposed rule isn't authority. Maybe they expect final rule, MSPB rule, and perhaps the OPM final rule's correction? Hmm. Let's think. Notice issued Aug 31, 2026; separation Oct 30, 2026. Under main RIF final rule DATES, if RIF notice before Sept 2, process under old rules. Under appeals final rule DATES, applies only to actions for which specific RIF notice under 351.802 on/after Sept 2. So MSPB. MSPB's 2026-16456 effective Sept 2 retains RIF appeals for actions taken before effective date. The OPM proposed rule 2026-02576 (Feb 10) proposed transfer from MSPB to OPM; if final not effective for pre-Sept 2 notices, proposed doesn't bear except context. Maybe 2026-15654? No. Could also be 5 U.S.C. 7701 etc., but not FR. Answer: MSPB. Cite 2026-15666 DATES (91 FR 49230), 2026-16456 DATES and §III (91 FR 51997-51998). Maybe mention 2026-02576 proposed rule as not controlling. To be safe, say "The 2026 documents that bear on this are the OPM RIF appeals final rule (2026-15666), its DATES; and the MSPB Appellate Jurisdiction Update II (2026-16456), DATES and section III. The proposed rule (2026-02576) is not authority."

Q7(b): OPM; e-file; deadline Jan 19, 2027 11:59 p.m. ET. Show counting. Note 30 calendar days from effective date Dec 18: Dec 19 day 1; Jan 17 day 30 (Sunday); Jan 18 MLK Day; first workday Jan 19. Good.

Q7(c): prove by preponderance: timeliness, jurisdiction, failure to comply with applicable statute or OPM RIF regulation, prejudice (action or loss of materially more favorable outcome). Hearing: not entitled; OPM may hold hearing if necessary and efficient; review based solely on written record otherwise. Cite 351.901(b), 351.905(c). Could also mention no entitlement to hearing; "when necessary and efficient" standard.

Q7(d): Rule says 351.901(c)(2) RIF action and any matter relating to appeal may not be raised under negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration. Preamble says final rule does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs or purport to adjudicate particular CBA disputes; OPM does not adopt position that proposal would automatically vitiate existing agreements mid-term; when agreements renegotiated, rule limits duty/ability to bargain for inconsistent direct RIF appeal process; questions about effect of particular existing agreement provisions, negotiability disputes, ULPs remain for chapter 71 forum. Cite 91 FR 49245. Also 351.901(c)(1) sole/exclusive. Good.

Q7(e): No judicial review: 351.901(c)(4); 351.909(e) no further right of appeal; preamble 91 FR 49242-43 explains CSRA exclusivity. Answer no.

Q7(f): Yes, 351.902(b)(3); deadline April 9, 2027 (30 calendar days after March 10, 2027 final decision; March 11 day 1; April 9 day 30). Need mention that she must have timely filed the OSC complaint before expiration of her RIF appeal period (she did: before Jan 19, 2027). Also decision must materially affect retention standing etc.; OPM sole discretion. Good.

Q7(g): DATES of 2026-15666, 91 FR 49230: applies only to RIF action for which agency issues specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after Sept 2, 2026. Also preamble 91 FR 49248 says applicability stated in preamble and not in 351.901. The exact provision deciding between (a) and (b) is this applicability sentence. Cite also 2026-16456 DATES. Good.

Q8 details: Need current 351.806 version: "when possible" language. But what does it say exactly? The preamble quotes revised text and says change from "when possible." We can say "as it applies today, the pre-November 18 text (the version referenced in the preamble as using 'when possible') provided that, when possible, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period, with the other provisions on emergency lack of work or funds." But the exact current text of paragraphs (b), (c) unknown. Could state only what documents show: preamble at 91 FR 65925-26 says paragraph (a) "retains the general expectation" and "replaces the 'when possible' language"; 91 FR 65933 says change from "when possible" to "under ordinary circumstances." And 2026-21320 republishes entire 351.806; the new text includes (a), (b), (c). The pre-existing version's (c) emergency provision is "longstanding" and appears in final at (c) only because restructured (91 FR 65936). So current version likely has similar emergency provision. But task says if a paragraph isn't printed, say so. We can answer: Today, the version in force is the pre-November 18 text, which OPM describes as using "when possible" for the duty-status presumption; the 2026 documents do not print the full current text. The adopted but not yet in force version is 2026-21320's revision, effective Nov 18, 2026, printed at 91 FR 65939: (a) under ordinary circumstances duty status; (b) administrative leave permitted if appropriate and consistent with part 630 subpart N; (c) emergency lack of work/funds annual leave etc. Good.

Q8(b): Adopted text + companion leave provision: no consent needed ("placing" an employee; "provide" includes without consent; 630.1403(c)(10)); no explicit limit in 351.806(b) or 630.1403(c)(10). But "consistent with part 630, subpart N" includes 630.1403(a)(3) (usually not more than 1 workday, longer when appropriate). OPM policy's governmentwide 12-week limit for administrative leave in connection with a "workforce realignment initiative" (CPM 2025-12) may apply; but is a RIF notice period a workforce realignment initiative? OPM's preamble at 65926 and 65927 says "workforce-realignment uses in Sec. 630.1403(c)(9) and (c)(11)" are expressly subject to limits; (c)(10) RIF not expressly. Hmm. The 12-week limit is stated as applying to "administrative leave ... in connection with a workforce realignment initiative." A RIF is a workforce realignment initiative. Could answer: no consent; no explicit durational limit in the regulatory text, but use must be consistent with subpart N, including the principle in 630.1403(a)(3) that administrative leave is usually for not more than one workday and longer only when appropriate; OPM's governmentwide policy limits workforce realignment administrative leave to 12 weeks per instance unless higher threshold jointly approved (preamble 91 FR 65926, 65935). But the question likely expects "no consent, and no limit" or "12 weeks." Let's parse wording: "Under the adopted text and its companion leave provision, is employee consent needed, and is there a limit on how long this leave may last?" Companion leave provision = 630.1403(c)(10). It says "To provide administrative leave to employees subject to an involuntary separation via a RIF during the period between receipt of the RIF notice and the RIF separation when the agency determines it is in the Government's best interests." No consent, no explicit limit. But it is subject to 630.1403(a)(3) generally. Could say: consent not required; neither provision sets a specific maximum duration, but the leave must satisfy subpart N's general principles (630.1403(a)), including that administrative leave is ordinarily for not more than one workday and longer periods only in appropriate circumstances; the 12-week Governmentwide limit discussed in the preamble applies to "workforce realignment initiative" leave, and OPM does not state that it is incorporated into (c)(10). This is a defensible nuanced answer. Maybe mention 351.806(b) itself says "all or part of the notice period"; notice period could be up to 60 days or more. Hmm.

Q8(c): OPM says before adopted text, agency policy guidance allowed administrative leave between notice and separation; specifically section D.1.b of Agency Policy Template (CPM 2025-12, July 30, 2025), and the final rule's new 351.806(b) "regulatory clarification is consistent with OPM policy guidance which already provided that an authorized agency official may provide administrative leave between an employee's receipt of a notice of involuntary separation and the effective date of that separation" (91 FR 65926). Also 5 U.S.C. 6329a and part 630 subpart N. Good.

Q8(d): No—preamble 91 FR 65926: does not alter RIF requirements; retention registers, retention standing, veterans' preference, appeal rights continue to apply in full; nothing authorizes bypass. Also 351.806(a)/(b) only duty status. Good.

Now Q10: done.

Now Q1 details:
(a) doc 2026-15665; citation 91 FR 49178-49227; published Aug 3, 2026; effective Sept 2, 2026; docket OPM-2025-0107; RIN 3206-AO86.
(b) proposed rule 2026-04377; 91 FR 10904-10934; published March 5, 2026; comments closed May 4.
(c) corrections: 2026-17335, published Aug 25, 2026, effective Sept 2, 2026 — corrects typographical/clerical errors in amendatory instructions and regulatory text (e.g., instructions 15, 36, 39; "of this part" references; list structure; citation errors; conforms authority citation to appeals rule). 2026-18800, published Sept 15, 2026, effective Sept 15, 2026 — restores paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) of definition of "displaced" in 5 CFR 330.602 inadvertently removed by amendatory instruction 11. Need one line each. Note 2026-17335 corrects main rule; 2026-18800 corrects main rule (CFR 330). 
(d) DATES and Implementation.
(e) 2026-15666 (RIF Appeals) — adds subpart I (351.901-351.909), revises 351.802(a)(6), 351.807(e); effective Sept 2, 2026; in force today. 2026-21316 (Managing Senior Professional Performance) — revises 351.203 "Rating of record" and 351.503(a)(1), (b)(2)-(3) to incorporate part 430 subpart E senior professional summary levels; effective Nov 18, 2026; not in force today. 2026-21320 (Administrative Leave) — revises 351.806; effective Nov 18, 2026; not in force today. Maybe mention 2026-13715 (effective Aug 6, 2026) excluded because before Sept 2; if asked "every other final rule published in 2026 through today that amends 5 CFR part 351 with effect on or after the main rule's effective date," maybe 2026-13715's effect is before, so not included. But it did amend part 351—what did it do? Maybe 351.503 references to 430.208(e)? Let's quickly check its part 351 amendment; could matter for Q11? Q11 compares proposed vs final of main rule; 2026-13715 was before main rule. Perhaps final main rule references "prior to final rule at 91 FR 41521" because of it. Not needed.

Let's search 2026-13715 for "351." to know.

Important: 2026-13715 amended 351.504 to change references from 430.208(d) to 430.208(e), effective Aug 6, 2026. It's before main rule effective date but it amended part 351. Q1(e) excludes because effect before main rule's effective date. But maybe list mention? The question: "List every other final rule published in 2026, through today, that amends 5 CFR part 351 (not counting corrections) with effect on or after the main rule's effective date." 2026-13715 effect Aug 6, so not list. But in basis maybe note it exists but is outside because effective before. Fine.

Now Q11: Must compare proposed vs final regulatory text. Note 2026-13715 changed 351.504 references before main rule; proposed main rule used 430.208(d), final uses 430.208(e) (because 2026-13715 changed it). That's a difference between proposed and final, but perhaps considered a cross-reference change. Q11 says cross-reference pointing to different section/subpart/part counts, but 430.208(d) vs (e) is different paragraph; yes include.

Need read proposed 351.705/802 end and final already. Good.

Need check proposed 351.202(d) wording exactly; have it.

Let's now think about Q13 more systematically. Perhaps the intended answer is a set of preamble misstatements. Let's search main rule preamble for phrases that conflict with text: "temporary appointment", "veteran", "three grades", "351.201(a)(2)", "date of the RIF notice", "180 days", "351.602". We found:
1. Erosion of duties: 91 FR 49190 says modifying 351.201(a)(2), 180 days; text 351.202(c)(3), adverse effect.
2. Excluded appointments: 91 FR 49191 says competitive and excepted employees serving temporary or time-limited appointments ≤1 year excluded; text 351.202(d)(2)(iii) only temporary under subpart D; another passage 49191 correct.
3. Same: 91 FR 49196 says competitive service tenure group excludes "temporary or time-limited appointment"; text 351.502(a)(3) temporary under subpart D; another passage? 49191 correct as to competitive temporary only maybe.

content.text:
Great. Q14(ii): find proposed-to-final change not acknowledged in final rule's summary of changes from proposal. Let's compare:
- Proposed §351.901(a): "An employee who has been the subject of a reduction-in-force action may appeal an action taken under this part" -> final "furloughed for more than 30 days, separated, or demoted..." Acknowledged ("Clarifying appealable actions").
- Proposed (b)(1) "timeliness of the appeal" -> final "timeliness of the written appeal" (minor, not acknowledged? maybe). Proposed (b)(2) "OPM possesses jurisdiction" -> final "That OPM possesses jurisdiction"; minor.
- Proposed (b)(3) two-part? changed to (3)+(4) two-part showing; acknowledged ("Revising the merits standard").
- Proposed (c) "shall supersede any appeal procedures found in agency policies or collective bargaining agreements, but they do not otherwise preclude ... EEOC, FLRA, IG, MSPB, DOL VETS, OSC." Final (c)(1)-(4): "sole and exclusive means"; (c)(2) may not raise under negotiated grievance procedure or contest through grievance arbitration; (c)(3) preserves EEOC, IG, MSPB, DOL VETS, OSC (FLRA removed); (c)(4) no judicial review. Summary acknowledges "Revising exclusivity language" but does it acknowledge removal of FLRA from preserved entities? Summary says "expressly preserving collateral matters within independent jurisdiction of EEOC, Inspectors General, MSPB, DOL VETS, and OSC." It does not mention removing FLRA. Proposed preserved FLRA; final doesn't. That's a proposed-to-final change not acknowledged! Great Q14(ii) candidate. But is it real? Proposed (c) included "Federal Labor Relations Authority"; final 351.901(c)(3) omits FLRA. The summary's listing of preserved entities omits FLRA, so perhaps implicitly acknowledged? But it doesn't say it removed FLRA. Q14(ii) asks "a change from proposed appeals rule to final appeals rule that the final rule's summary of its changes from the proposal (near the start of its preamble) does not acknowledge." This is a strong candidate: removal of FLRA from the list of forums in which collateral matters may be filed.
- Proposed §351.902(a): "[URL TBD]" -> final "system identified on OPM's website"; acknowledged.
- Proposed (b) "Eastern Standard Time" -> final "Eastern Time"; acknowledged.
- Proposed (b)(2) and (3) separate: (2) untimely dismissed unless good cause; (3) good cause sole discretion. Final consolidates into (b)(2); acknowledged ("consolidates the untimely-filing rule").
- Final adds (b)(3) tolling; acknowledged.
- Proposed (c)(2): no exception for good cause/exemption? Final (c)(2) adds "or exempted under paragraph (c)(7) for good cause." Summary says "more flexible reply rules"? Actually summary e-filing section says "narrows e-filing enforcement" but doesn't mention adding exemption cross-reference. Minor.
- Proposed (c)(4): broad orders/sanctions/termination; final narrows to strike document after repeated failure/show cause; acknowledged.
- Proposed (c)(6): includes "may preclude future re-registering"; final removes; acknowledged ("also removes the proposed statement that withdrawal from e-filing may preclude future re-registration...").
- Proposed (c)(7) same.
- Proposed §351.903(a): "legal name, best address" -> final "name, address"; acknowledged ("Simplifying initial-appeal information").
- Proposed §351.903(b): flat list; final structured (b)(1)-(4), adds minimum agency record, production vs service; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.903(c): reply 15 days; final adds exceptions for new allegations; acknowledged ("Allowing limited new matters in reply").
- Proposed §351.903(d) inspection with no limits; final adds limits; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.903(e) service with no limits; final adds limits; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.904: one paragraph; final (a)-(c) reorganized, narrows disallowance grounds; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.905(a): assignment restrictions; final adds adjudicator insulation and ex parte safeguards; acknowledged. But final also changes "When necessary, OPM may appoint an administrative law judge" to "may assign"; minor.
- Proposed §351.905(b): OPM employee appeals: final adds "material factual error that affected outcome"; acknowledged ("adds material factual error affecting the outcome as a ground"). Final also adds "and clarifies that assigning an ALJ does not make 5 U.S.C. 554, 556, or 557 applicable..." acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.905(c): audit/investigation standard; final tightens; acknowledged. Final also adds requirement to inform/notify; proposed had same.
- Proposed §351.905(d): failure to participate in ascertainment sanction; final removes and renumbers; acknowledged ("Removing a separate ascertainment sanction").
- Proposed §351.905(e) initial decision -> final (d); proposed (f) remedies -> final (e). Reorganization not explicitly acknowledged? "renumbers" maybe.
- Proposed §351.906(a): narrower; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.906(b): "shall" -> final "may"; minor not acknowledged? Could be a change in discretion. Proposed: "OPM shall, except when prohibited by law: draw inferences..." Final: "OPM may, except when prohibited by law..." That's a substantive change from mandatory to discretionary sanctions, not mentioned in summary (summary says "narrows the standard..."). Q14(ii) candidate. Summary says "Refining protective-order authority" and "sanctions" maybe not. Could count.
- Proposed §351.907(a): "Upon a request from either party ... OPM may ... reopen" -> final "Upon a request from either party ... or upon its own initiative" — acknowledged ("Clarifying OPM-initiated reconsideration").
- Proposed §351.908: broad discretion -> final adds considerations, no party right; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.909(a): final changes finality structure; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.909(e): "publicly accessible website ... Any final decision not made publicly available shall be made available upon request by a concerned party. For purposes of this subsection, a concerned party means..." Final adds legal limits and "need to know" for agency representative; summary acknowledges public-posting disclosure limits, but does it acknowledge that agency representative must have "need to know"? It says "or a representative of the Federal agency or office involved in the proceeding who has a need to know." Summary: "It also clarifies that final merits decisions not publicly posted because of such legal limits must be made available upon request to the Federal employee or former Federal employee involved in a proceeding under this subpart, his or her representative..., or a representative of the Federal agency or office involved in the proceeding who has a need to know." So acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.901(c) removes FLRA; strong.

- Proposed §351.904(c): final removes "priority needs of Government" and "unreasonable costs" grounds; summary acknowledges ("does not adopt proposed additional grounds").
- Proposed §351.905(a): final adds insulation/ex parte; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.905(b): final adds material factual error; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.905(c): final adds "may require either party to provide additional information" (proposed didn't say that? Proposed only audit/investigate; final adds). Summary says "Tightening audits and investigations" but not the new authority to require information. Maybe.
- Proposed §351.906(b) "shall" -> "may": not acknowledged. Good candidate.
- Proposed §351.907(a): final adds "or upon its own initiative"; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.909(e): final adds legal limits; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.901(a): final changes "subject of a RIF action" to enumerated actions; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.902(a): final replaces "statements" with "pleadings"; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.903(a): final changes "legal name, best address" to "name, address"; acknowledged.
- Proposed §351.905(a): final removes "appoint" -> "assign"; minor.

- Proposed §351.901(c) final says "procedures in this part" (later corrected to "this subpart") vs proposed "this part"; correction; not summary.
- Proposed §351.902(b)(3) tolling says entity identified in 351.901(c) but final corrected (c)(3); summary says 351.901(c). Not.

Search summary for "FLRA" and "shall"/"may". The summary at lines 108-336 doesn't mention FLRA. It mentions "preserving collateral matters within independent jurisdiction of EEOC, Inspectors General, MSPB, DOL VETS, and OSC" (line 154-158) — this actually lists the final preserved entities and thus implicitly acknowledges FLRA not included. Hmm, but it doesn't say "removed FLRA." Q14(ii) says "a change ... that the final rule's summary of its changes from the proposal ... does not acknowledge." The list omitting FLRA could be seen as acknowledging the final set. But not explicitly. Maybe too risky. The "shall" -> "may" sanctions change is clearly not acknowledged; the summary says "Refining protective-order authority" but not changing mandatory to discretionary. Is that a "change from proposed to final" worth listing? Yes.

Another: Proposed §351.902(c)(2) says no party may file/access unless registered; final adds "or exempted under paragraph (c)(7) for good cause." Summary does mention "more flexible reply rules" but not e-filing exemption; but it does mention "good cause requirement permits nonelectronic filing methods" in section-by-section. The summary's e-filing paragraph doesn't mention. Could be candidate.

Another: Proposed §351.901(a) "subject of a reduction-in-force action" -> final enumerated. Acknowledged.

Another: Proposed §351.902(b) "within 30 calendar days from effective date" -> final same.

Another: Proposed §351.904 "An employee may select..." -> final "An appellant may select..." minor.

query.description: Full-text search terms; "" for none. Supports quoted phrases, e.g. "\"extension of stay\" F-1".

doc_type.description: Document types: RULE, PRORULE (proposed rule), NOTICE, PRESDOCU (presidential document). null for all.

agency.description: Agency slugs, e.g. homeland-security-department, u-s-citizenship-and-immigration-services, u-s-immigration-and-customs-enforcement, state-department, labor-department, executive-office-of-the-president.
agency.title: Agency

pres_type.description: Presidential document subtypes (use with doc_type PRESDOCU).

cfr.description: CFR title:part affected, e.g. 8:214. The part must be numeric; lettered parts are not supported by this filter.

tools.description: Search U.S. Federal Register documents (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) by keywords and filters. Prints document numbers, titles, types, dates, citations, dockets, RINs and abstracts.

tools.name: fr_doc
tools.description: Metadata for one Federal Register document: title, type, action, citation, page range, publication/signing/effective dates, comment deadline, docket, RIN, CFR parts affected, corrections, abstract.

tools.name: fr_toc
tools.description: Outline of a document's full text: headings with line numbers. Output may contain CLI-style hints such as '--start N' or '--max'; they refer to this tool's parameters.

pattern.description: Python regular expression, searched over the whole text (a match may span lines). ^ and $ match at line boundaries; . does not match a newline.

context.description: Lines of context around each match (default 2, at most 10).

basis.description: Provisions and documents relied on, with citations.

uncertainty.description: What the documents leave open, or "None".
uncertainty.title: Uncertainty

1. **351.202(d)(2)(iii)**: proposed excluded a “temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316”; final excludes only “a temporary appointment of one (1) year or less under subpart D of part 316.”
2. **351.202(d)(3)–(4)**: proposed said covered employees “may be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted or reassigned without regard to the provisions of this part”; final states they are not competing employees, specifies the actions may be taken without retention-standing/order-of-release/assignment-right determinations, and adds (d)(4), requiring a modified notice under 351.801 with specified 351.802 content.

4. **351.203 “Rating of record”**: proposed cross-referenced Sec. 430.208(d); final cross-references Sec. 430.208(e).

(a) **A**: not a preference eligible; **0 points**; Subgroup **B**. 351.504(b)(1) not met (length-of-service retirement, no disability); (b)(2) not met (22 years); (b)(3) not met; (b)(4) fails because not a disabled veteran. **B**: not a preference eligible; **0 points**; Subgroup **B**. Retirement pay is based on 21 years’ active service, so (b)(2) is not met; (b)(1) is not met because retirement is not based on disability; (b)(4) requires meeting (b)(1)–(3). **C**: preference eligible; **5 points**; Subgroup **AD**. Disability retirement for injury in the line of duty as a direct result of armed conflict satisfies 351.504(b)(1), and major is “major or above” under (b)(4). **D**: not a preference eligible; **0 points**; Subgroup **B**. 351.504(b)(2) not met (24 years), rank below major, no disability. **E**: preference eligible; **3 points**; Subgroup **A**. Although the 10% disability is not from armed conflict or an instrumentality of war, retired pay is not based on 20 or more years of full-time active service, so 351.504(b)(2) is met; because the disability is under 30%, 351.504(a)(2) gives 3 points.
(b) **A**: not a preference eligible, so under 351.505(b)(2)(i) only the 2 years of campaign-badge service count; SCD = Sept. 7, 2010 − 2 years = **Sept. 7, 2008**. **C**: preference eligible, so 351.505(b)(2)(ii) credits total active service (14 years); SCD = Sept. 7, 2010 − 14 years = **Sept. 7, 1996**.
(c) The AD/A/B subgroups do not independently order retention. Q5.answer:
(a)(i) Notice **Aug. 28, 2026** is before Sept. 2, so the earlier rules apply (91 FR 49178, 49207). Under them, Level 5 = 20 years and Level 3 = 12 years additional service; Lee: (12+12+12)/3 = 12 years, adjusted SCD Mar. 2, 1986; Park: (20+20+20)/3 = 20 years, adjusted SCD July 8, 1999. Both are Group I/Subgroup B; earlier adjusted SCD wins, so **Park is released**. (ii) Notice **Sept. 2, 2026** is on the effective date, so the amended rules apply: Lee 3+3+3 = **9**; Park 7+7+7 = **21**; **Lee is released**. (iii) Notice **Sept. 3, 2026**: same amended rules; **Lee is released**.
(b) **No recalculation.** The Sept. 3 notice fixed retention standing as of receipt (351.507(a)). An amended notice solely moving the effective date to a later date is not a new specific RIF notice and does not require redetermination or recalculation of retention standing under subpart E (351.805(b)). Lee’s Oct. 15 Level 5 rating therefore does not change the result; Lee remains released.
(c) (1) **Which version applies**: the date the agency **issues** the RIF notice — DATES, 91 FR 49178, and Implementation, 91 FR 49207. (2) **End of the four-year ratings period**: the date of issuance of RIF notices, or the agency’s cutoff date if one is used — 351.503(c)(1)–(2). (3) **Tenure subgroup and retention standing**: the date the employee **receives** a specific RIF notice — 351.502(a)(2)–(3), (b)(2)–(3); 351.507(a).

Q6.answer:
(a) Jordan has assignment rights to positions **1 (GS-12 Ellis)**, **2 (GS-11 Frank)**, and **3 (GS-10 Gale)**: each is in the same competitive area, has the same full-time work schedule, is held by an employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group, and is within three grades of GS-13 (351.701(a), (b)). The agency **must offer position 1**, because it requires the least reduction in representative rate. Position 4 (GS-9) is four grades below GS-13, outside the three-grade limit; position 5 (Ito) is held by a higher-standing employee; position 6 (Kim) is part-time, not the same type of work schedule; position 7 (Lund) is in a different competitive area.
(b) With a compensable 30%+ disability, the grade limit becomes **five grades**, so position 4 (GS-9) also becomes within reach (351.701(b)(2)); the mandatory offer is still **position 1**, the least reduction.
(c) If Jordan’s current annual rating is **Level 1**, 351.701(a) does not apply: only an employee with a current annual rating of Level 2 or higher has assignment rights. He has **no assignment right** to any of the positions.
(d) In the excepted service, 351.701 does not apply by its terms (it covers a “competitive service tenure group employee”). An agency may, in its discretion, adopt provisions giving excepted-service employees assignment rights on the same basis under 351.705(a); absent such agency action, there is **no mandatory assignment right**.
(e) The handbook’s “Level 2 cannot take a position held by someone with a higher rating” statement reflects the former Sec. 351.701(d), which the final rule **eliminated** because it was no longer necessary; 351.701(a) now permits assignment for a Level 2 or higher employee, subject to the other requirements (91 FR 49204). The separate “bumping” and “retreating” concepts were also replaced: assignment rights now run to a position held by an employee with lower retention standing in the same tenure group, without the old bump/retreat distinction (91 FR 49204; 351.701(b)).

Q7.answer:
(a) **The Merit Systems Protection Board** hears the appeal. The OPM appeals rule applies only to a RIF action for which the agency issues a specific RIF notice under 351.802 **on or after Sept. 2, 2026** (2026-15666, DATES, 91 FR 49230). The MSPB’s Appellate Jurisdiction Update II (2026-16456) is effective Sept. 2, 2026 but states that MSPB will continue to adjudicate RIF appeals relating to actions taken before that date, including cases where the RIF notice was issued before the rule’s effective date (91 FR 51997–51998). The proposed appeals rule (2026-02576) is not authority.
(b) **OPM** hears the appeal. Morgan must file through the electronic filing system identified on OPM’s website (351.902(a)). Deadline: 30 calendar days from the Dec. 18, 2026 effective date; the first day counted is Dec. 19, 2026; the 30th day is Sunday, Jan. 17, 2027; Jan. 18, 2027 is the Martin Luther King, Jr. Federal holiday; the first workday is **Tuesday, Jan. 19, 2027**, and the appeal is timely if e-filed by **11:59 p.m. Eastern Time** that day (351.902(b), (b)(1)).
(c) She must prove by a preponderance of the evidence: timeliness; OPM jurisdiction; that the agency failed to comply with an applicable statute or OPM RIF regulation; and that the failure prejudiced her by causing the appealed action or the loss of a materially more favorable outcome (351.901(b)). She is **not entitled to a hearing as of right**; review is on the written record unless OPM determines a hearing is “necessary and efficient” (351.905(c)).
(d) The rule bars the union’s grievance: a RIF action and any matter relating to an appeal of it “may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration” (351.901(c)(2)). The preamble says the final rule does **not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs** or adjudicate particular CBA disputes; OPM does not adopt the position that the proposal would automatically vitiate existing agreements mid-term; when agreements are renegotiated, the governmentwide rule will limit bargaining for a direct RIF appeal process inconsistent with part 351; questions about particular existing agreement provisions, negotiability disputes, or unfair-labor-practice allegations remain for resolution under chapter 71 (91 FR 49245).
(e) **No.** A party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under subpart I (351.901(c)(4)); there is no further right of appeal of a final OPM decision (351.909(e)); the preamble explains the CSRA exclusivity (91 FR 49242–49243).
(f) **Yes.** Because she timely filed an OSC complaint before the RIF appeal period expired and the final decision on that matter materially affects her retention standing, she may file a RIF appeal within 30 calendar days after the decision becomes final and no longer subject to further administrative review (351.902(b)(3)). The March 10, 2027 final decision gives a deadline of **April 9, 2027** (March 11 is day 1; April 9 is day 30), e-filed by 11:59 p.m. ET. OPM determines in its sole discretion whether the decision materially affects her rights.
(g) The controlling provision is the **DATES** sentence of 2026-15666 at **91 FR 49230**: “This final rule applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026.”

Q8.answer:
(a) **Today (Nov. 14, 2026)**, 5 CFR 351.806 is the pre-amendment version, which OPM describes as using “when possible” for the duty-status presumption; the 2026 documents do not print its full current text (the preamble at 91 FR 65925–65926 and 65933 describes the change from “when possible” to “under ordinary circumstances”). **Adopted but not yet in force**: 2026-21320, effective **Nov. 18, 2026**, revises 351.806 to read: (a) under ordinary circumstances an employee remains in duty status during the notice period; (b) nothing precludes an agency from placing an employee on administrative leave for all or part of the notice period when appropriate and consistent with part 630, subpart N; (c) emergency lack of work or funds permits annual leave with or without consent, leave without pay with consent, or nonpay status without consent (91 FR 65939).
(b) **No employee consent is required** to place an employee on administrative leave under 351.806(b); the preamble says “provide” covers administrative leave “with or without the employee’s consent” (91 FR 65933). Neither 351.806(b) nor the companion 630.1403(c)(10) states a fixed maximum duration; the leave must satisfy subpart N’s general principles (including 630.1403(a)(3): usually not more than one workday, longer only when appropriate). OPM’s governmentwide policy limit of 12 weeks per instance for administrative leave in connection with a workforce realignment initiative is discussed in the preamble (91 FR 65926, 65935), but 630.1403(c)(10) does not expressly incorporate it.
(c) OPM says its policy guidance — section D.1.b of the Agency Policy Template (CPM 2025-12, July 30, 2025) — already provided that an authorized agency official may provide administrative leave between an employee’s receipt of a notice of involuntary separation and the effective date of separation; the rule merely codifies that existing guidance (91 FR 65926 & n.3).
(d) **No.** OPM states that the new 630.1403(c)(10) and revised 351.806 address only paid non-duty status and do not alter RIF competition, retention registers, retention standing, veterans’ preference, notice, or appeal rights; nothing authorizes bypassing RIF procedures (91 FR 65926).
Q8.uncertainty: The exact full text of the current pre-Nov. 18 version of 351.806 is not printed; also, whether the 12-week policy limit applies to RIF-notice administrative leave under 630.1403(c)(10) is not expressly resolved.

Q9.answer:
**In order: Steps 2, 7 and 9.** **Do not comply: Steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11 and 12.**
- **Step 1 — noncompliant.** The Tulsa Field Office is an organizational unit on the official chart and was approved by the agency head’s designee, which is permitted, but it was established **Aug. 17, 2026**, fewer than 90 days before the **Oct. 13, 2026** notices. The agency therefore had to submit a description and written statement of bona fide organizational basis to OPM for approval in advance; nothing was sent (351.402(b)(1), (c)).
- **Step 2 — in order.** A career-conditional employee serving the initial probationary period is not a competing employee and may be retained while a competing employee is released (351.202(d)(2)(ii), (d)(3)).
- **Step 3 — noncompliant.** A supervisory probationary period is not an “initial probationary period” (351.203, definition), so Ms. Ortiz must be included and ranked in competitive service tenure subgroup I; the agency must not omit her merely because she is on supervisory probation.
- **Step 4 — noncompliant.** The 30-day cutoff was **Sept. 13, 2026**; the Oct. 2, 2026 rating was received after the cutoff and cannot be used. The agency also violated the uniform-and-consistent requirement by using a later rating for only one employee (351.503(c)(2), (c)(3), (c)(4)).
- **Step 5 — noncompliant.** For two ratings, the missing-rating proxy is (7+5)/2 = **6**, so Ms. Quist’s credit is 7+5+6 = **18**, not 15 (351.503(f)(2)).
- **Step 6 — noncompliant.** Additional points for performance are permitted only under the single-rating-pattern rule for a pattern whose highest level is Level 3, and only for documented exceptional performance; they are not authorized as a 2-point add-on for QSI recipients under a five-level pattern (351.503(d), (e)).
- **Step 7 — in order.** When employees are tied on augmented performance credit, tenure subgroup and SCD, the agency may select any tied employee for release (351.601(c)).
- **Step 8 — noncompliant.** The agency may not release a competing employee from a competitive level while retaining an employee in that level with a specifically limited temporary or term promotion (351.602(a)).
- **Step 9 — in order.** No new assessment is required where, during the five years ending on the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice, the employee held the same position (or same grade/pay level with substantially the same duties, series, qualifications and conditions) and received a Level 3 or higher rating for those duties (351.702(a)(4)(v)).
- **Step 10 — noncompliant.** An assessment may not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment; the agency must use a job-analysis-based assessment allowing demonstration of job-related skills, abilities, knowledge and competencies (351.702(a)(4)(i)–(iii)).
- **Step 11 — noncompliant.** Temporary exceptions may not be sequenced or stacked; the agency may use one exception, and if more than one is available, the one providing the longest retention, not 60 days plus another 60 days (351.608(a)(3); 351.608(b) and (g) each allow up to 90 days).
- **Step 12 — noncompliant.** For a RIF noticed on Oct. 13, 2026, the appeal is to **OPM**, not MSPB. The notice must state the right to appeal to OPM, the time limit under 351.902(b), and the electronic filing system (351.802(a)(6), as amended by 2026-15666; 351.901).

Q10.answer:
(a) On **Sept. 10, 2026**, paragraph (1) of the definition of “displaced” in 5 CFR 330.602 contained **only the introductory text** — “A current competitive service employee in the competitive service tenure group at grade GS-15 (or equivalent) or below (or another qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM) who:” — with **no subparagraphs (i) or (ii)**. Amendatory instruction 11 of 2026-15665 set out only the introductory text as the revised paragraph, which inadvertently deleted (1)(i) and (1)(ii).
(b) **2026-18800**, published and effective **Sept. 15, 2026**, restored paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) as they read before the final rule. OPM acted without notice and comment under the good-cause exception of **5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B)**, stating that the correction makes **no substantive change** — it restores text in effect before Sept. 2, 2026 that OPM did not propose to remove and the final rule did not discuss removing — and made it effective upon publication under 553(d)(3) (91 FR 58363–58364).
(c) After the correction, under paragraph (1)(i): if Nadia is offered a full-time position with a **lower** representative rate than her present full-time position and declines, she has **not** declined an offer of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as her present position, so she **remains “displaced.”** If the offered position had the **same** representative rate (and same work schedule), declining it would mean she has declined a qualifying offer, and she would **not** be “displaced” under paragraph (1)(i).

Q11.answer:
Real differences between the proposed and final part 351 regulatory text (paragraph; proposed → final):
1. **351.202(d)(2)(iii)**: proposed excluded a “temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316”; final excludes only “a temporary appointment of one (1) year or less under subpart D of part 316.”
2. **351.202(d)(3)–(4)**: proposed said covered employees “may be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted or reassigned without regard to the provisions of this part”; final states they are not competing employees, specifies the actions may be taken without retention-standing/order-of-release/assignment-right determinations, and adds (d)(4), requiring a modified notice under 351.801 with specified 351.802 content.
3. **351.203 “Furlough”**: proposed added “and is instead dependent entirely on congressional action, rather than agency action”; final omits that clause.
4. **351.203 “Rating of record”**: proposed cross-referenced Sec. 430.208(d); final cross-references Sec. 430.208(e).
5. **351.204**: proposed required only following/applying the regulations; final adds the responsibility to ensure they are administered and applied consistent with all applicable laws, including the merit system principles in 5 U.S.C. 2301(b).
6. **351.302(d)**: proposed required use of part 752 adverse-action procedures; final adds “or other procedures required by law, regulation, or the terms of the employee’s appointment.”
7. **351.402**: proposed revised only paragraph (b); final also revises paragraph (c), adding the requirement to submit a competitive-area description and bona fide organizational explanation to OPM for approval when a competitive area is established or materially modified within 90 days before specific RIF notices.
8. **351.502**: proposed measured tenure subgroup status “as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice”; final measures it “as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice” (subgroup I and II, competitive and excepted).
9. **351.502(a)(3)**: proposed excluded a “temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316”; final excludes only “a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D of part 316.”
10. **351.503(a)(1)**: proposed referenced “patterns of summary level in Sec. 430.208(d)”; final references “5 CFR 430.208(e).”
11. **351.503(d) and (e)(2)**: final adds the authorization clause for pattern A/pass-fail or pattern D systems “authorized under [Sec. 430.208(d)] prior to the final rule prescribed at 91 FR 41521” (as corrected by 2026-17335); proposed had no such clause.
12. **351.504(a)**: proposed said the AD/A/B subgroups “should be identified”; final says “must be identified.”
13. **351.505(b)(2)**: proposed said “a retired member … covered by Sec. 351.503(b)”; final says “covered by Sec. 351.504(b).”
14. **351.506(c)(2)**: proposed cross-referenced “Sec. 351.701(b) and (c)”; final, as corrected, cross-references only “Sec. 351.701(b).”
15. **351.506(d)**: final adds that an employee who has not received a specific RIF notice has no right under the section, but that this does not limit access under another statute or regulation; proposed had no such sentence.
16. **351.604**: proposed would have revised paragraph (b) and removed paragraph (d) (RIF furlough criteria); final did not adopt those amendments.
17. **351.605**: proposed combined the abolishment rule and notice in paragraph (b); final restructures into (a) appropriate use, (b) abolishment, (c) notice (with a written notice under 351.801 and identification of the competitive area being abolished), and (d) retention register not required (and “must not” apply assignment rights).
18. **351.606(a)**: proposed gave a general retention priority under Sec. 351.209(b); final adds detailed mandatory-exception rules in (a)(1)–(6), including first determining ordinary retention standing, reassignment when an entire competitive area is abolished, OPM placement assistance, and documentation.
19. **351.608(a)(2)**: proposed cross-referenced CTAP at part 330, subpart E; final cross-references subpart F.
20. **351.702(a)(4)**: final adds paragraph (v), the exception from the assessment requirement for an employee who held the same or substantially similar position within five years and received a Level 3 or higher rating; proposed had no equivalent.
21. **351.802**: final adds introductory text to paragraph (a) and changes proposed “veteran status” to “veterans’ preference subgroup,” and proposed “A link to part 351 … and access to the agency’s records” to “A link to 5 CFR part 351 and information on how to access the agency’s records.”
22. **351.805(b)**: final adds the rule that an amended notice solely stating a later effective date is not a new specific RIF notice and does not require redetermination/recalculation of retention standing; proposed contained no such amendment.
Q11.uncertainty: The list covers differences I could verify from the printed regulatory text; it omits purely stylistic changes and may not capture every non-substantive wording change.

Q12.answer:
(a) **Register (GS-13 level):**
- **Alvarez**: 7+7+5 = **19**; preference 0; total **19**; career = subgroup I.
- **Chen**: the Sept. 30, 2022 Level 2 is outside the four-year period beginning Oct. 5, 2022; two ratings remain, Nov. 14, 2024 Level 5 (7) and Nov. 13, 2025 Level 4 (5); proxy = (7+5)/2 = 6; credit = **18**; preference 0; total **18**; subgroup I.
- **Dube**: 5+5 = 10; proxy = 5; performance 15; preference +3; total **18**; career-conditional after probation = subgroup II.
- **Estrada**: the Oct. 20, 2026 Level 5 is after the Oct. 5 notice and is not used; ratings Nov. 2023 Level 4 (5), Nov. 2024 Level 3 (3), Nov. 2025 Level 4 (5) = 13; preference +3; total **16**; subgroup I.
- **Brandt**: 3+5+0 = 8; 30%+ disabled preference +5; total **13**; subgroup I.
- **Farouk**: one actual rating Level 3; 3 × 3 = **9**; preference 0; total **9**; subgroup I. He is a **restoration protected employee** (restored July 13, 2026; 14 months’ uniformed service gives a one-year protection period under 38 U.S.C. 4316(c) and 351.203), so the mandatory exception in 351.606(a) applies.
- **Quinn**: **not on the register** — career-conditional serving the initial probationary period, excluded from RIF competition by 351.202(d)(2)(ii).
Order of retention: **Alvarez (19) > Chen (18, subgroup I) > Dube (18, subgroup II) > Estrada (16) > Brandt (13) > Farouk (9)**. Chen outranks Dube because both have 18 and subgroup I is ahead of subgroup II (351.501(c)).
(b) The three released are **Brandt, Estrada and Dube**, not Farouk. Farouk has the lowest score (9), but as a restoration protected employee he may not be released from the competitive level while another competing employee may be released instead (351.606(a)(2)); the agency must retain him and release the next lowest employees. Brandt is next lowest at 13; Estrada at 16; Dube at 18 (Dube is below Chen at the same 18 because Dube is subgroup II).
(c) **Brandt** (30%+ disabled; five-grade limit) has lower standing than Gomez (17), Hill (14) and Jones (15), but higher than Ikeda (9); he must be offered **Ikeda’s GS-9** position. **Estrada** (three-grade limit: GS-12, GS-11, GS-10) has lower standing than Gomez (17), but higher than Hill (14), Jones (15) and Ikeda (9); he must be offered **Hill’s GS-11**, the least reduction (not Jones’s GS-10). **Dube** has 18, higher than Gomez’s 17, so he must be offered **Gomez’s GS-12**, the least reduction. Dube cannot displace Chen (same 18 but Chen subgroup I), and Brandt cannot reach Gomez/Hill/Jones because their standing is higher.
(d) If all offers are accepted, the GS-13 employees remain; the displaced holders **Gomez, Hill and Ikeda** are released from their one-position competitive levels and, being qualified only for the positions they held, have no assignment rights and are **separated**.
Q12.uncertainty: Assumes Farouk’s 14 months of uniformed service is more than 180 days, giving a one-year protection period; even on the shorter six-month period, he would still be within protection on Oct. 5, 2026.

Q13.answer:
Preamble statements in 2026-15665 that differ from its own regulatory text:
1. **Erosion-of-duties amendment**: preamble at **91 FR 49190** says OPM is modifying **Sec. 351.201(a)(2)** to remove erosion-of-duties reclassifications “if the action would take effect after an agency had formally announced a RIF … and the RIF would take effect within 180 days.” The regulatory text instead amends **Sec. 351.202(c)(3)** at **91 FR 49218**, barring such a reclassification between formal announcement and completion of the RIF if it “would adversely affect an employee’s retention standing” — no 180-day condition. Another passage at **91 FR 49191** states the adverse-effect trigger correctly.
2. **Competitive-service temporary/time-limited exclusions**: preamble at **91 FR 49191** says “competitive and excepted service employees who are serving temporary or time-limited appointments of 1 year or less would be excluded from RIF competition.” The text at **91 FR 49218** (351.202(d)(2)(iii)) excludes only a **temporary** appointment of one year or less under part 316 subpart D for the competitive service; time-limited appointments are excluded only in the excepted service (351.202(d)(1)(i)). Another passage at **91 FR 49191** correctly notes that the final rule removed the proposed reference to term appointments and limits the competitive-service exclusion to temporary appointments under subpart D.
3. **Tenure group descriptions**: preamble at **91 FR 49196** says the competitive service tenure group excludes employees “as of the date of the RIF notice” serving “a temporary or time-limited appointment of 1 year or less,” and that subgroup II covers those not serving “a temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less.” The text at **91 FR 49220** measures status “as of the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice” and excludes only “a temporary appointment of 1 year or less under subpart D.” Another passage at **91 FR 49196** correctly uses “the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice” for subgroup I.
4. **“Preference eligible veteran”**: preamble at **91 FR 49197** says “each preference eligible veteran” receives 5 points and “every other preference eligible veteran” receives 3 points. The text at **91 FR 49221** (351.504(a)) applies to each “preference eligible employee” and every other “preference eligible employee”; preference eligibles include certain non-veteran family members. Another passage at **91 FR 49198** correctly notes that “preference eligibles” includes certain close family members of deceased or service-disabled veterans.
5. **Order of factors in examples**: preamble at **91 FR 49200** describes the final-rule order as “Tenure | Performance based on the total of the employee’s summary levels | Vets Pref | Service Computation Date.” The text at **91 FR 49220** (351.501(b)–(c)) makes performance credit **as augmented by veterans’ preference** the ranking factor, then uses tenure subgroup and SCD as tie-breakers. Another passage at **91 FR 49199** states that correctly.
6. **351.602 — appointment vs. promotion**: preamble at **91 FR 49202** says OPM is modifying Sec. 351.602 “to remove the prohibition on retaining an employee serving a specifically limited temporary appointment in a competitive level while releasing a competing employee.” The printed text at **91 FR 49223** still prohibits releasing a competing employee while retaining an employee with “a specifically limited temporary or term **promotion**.” No other passage states the point correctly.
7. **Grade limit for assignment rights**: preamble at **91 FR 49204** says a released employee has assignment rights to a position “not more than three grades below” the position from which released. The text at **91 FR 49225** (351.701(b)(2)) provides a **five-grade** limit for a preference eligible with a compensable service-connected disability of 30 percent or more. The Executive Summary at **91 FR 49178** states the five-grade exception correctly.
8. **Assessment exception — position and period**: Executive Summary item 13 at **91 FR 49178** says the assessment exception applies if the employee held “the same or substantially similar position within five years of the RIF” and received a Level 3 rating “for performing the duties of the position.” The text at **91 FR 49226** (351.702(a)(4)(v)) requires that, “during the 5-year period ending on the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice,” the employee occupied the same position, or a position at the same grade or pay level with substantially the same duties, occupational series, qualification requirements, and conditions, and received Level 3 or higher for those duties. Another passage at **91 FR 49204–49205** states the text accurately.
Q13.uncertainty: Some preamble statements are summaries rather than operative rules; I have listed only differences I could verify against the printed regulatory text.

Q14.answer:
(i) **Preamble vs. regulatory text of the OPM appeals rule**:
1. **Burden of proof — “required form”**: the preamble says the appellant must prove “that the written appeal was timely and in the required form” (**91 FR 49248**). The text, 351.901(b)(1) (**91 FR 49263**), requires proof only of “[t]he timeliness of the written appeal,” with no separate “required form” element.
2. **Inspection of the appellate record — omitted privileges**: the preamble says inspection is subject to the Privacy Act, classified-information/national-security requirements, protective orders, and “any other applicable limitation required by law” (**91 FR 49250**). The text, 351.903(d) (**91 FR 49265**), also subjects inspection to **applicable legal privileges**, which the preamble omits.
3. **Service — cross-reference to paragraph (b)**: the preamble says service is “subject to the disclosure limitations in paragraph (b)” (**91 FR 49250**). The text, 351.903(e) (**91 FR 49265**), does not cross-reference paragraph (b); it sets out its own list (Privacy Act, applicable legal privileges, classified/national-security requirements, OPM protective orders, and any other applicable disclosure limitation).
4. **“Responsible agency” in representation**: the preamble says OPM or the “responsible agency” may disallow a representative who is an employee of the “responsible agency or OPM” (**91 FR 49250**). As corrected, 351.904(c) (**91 FR 54796**) says “OPM or the agency whose action is under appeal” and “an employee of that agency or OPM”; the correction explains that “responsible agency” is undefined in part 351.
(ii) **Proposed-to-final changes not acknowledged in the summary near the start of the final preamble**:
1. **Removal of the FLRA from the preserved collateral forums**: proposed 351.901(c) preserved matters within the jurisdiction of the EEOC, **Federal Labor Relations Authority**, Inspector General, MSPB, DOL VETS and OSC (**91 FR 5875**). Final 351.901(c)(3) omits the FLRA and lists EEOC, Inspector General, MSPB, DOL VETS and OSC (**91 FR 49264**). The summary of changes discusses exclusivity and lists the preserved entities but does not acknowledge that the FLRA was dropped.
2. **Sanctions changed from mandatory to discretionary**: proposed 351.906(b) said OPM “shall” impose the listed consequences for failure to comply with a directive (**91 FR 5877**); final 351.906(b) says OPM “may” impose them (**91 FR 49266**). The summary’s “Refining protective-order authority” paragraph does not mention this change.
3. **E-filing exemption cross-reference added**: proposed 351.902(c)(2) barred filing/access unless registered as an e-filer; final 351.902(c)(2) adds “or exempted under paragraph (c)(7) of this section for good cause” (**91 FR 49264**). The summary’s e-filing discussion does not acknowledge this addition.
(iii) **Board/OPM inconsistency about which RIF appeals MSPB will still hear**:
1. **Within the Board’s rule**: the DATES and section I.B say MSPB will accept RIF appeals “where the agency’s RIF notice was issued before the rule’s effective date” (**91 FR 51997**), while section III says MSPB will adjudicate RIF appeals “in which the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026” (**91 FR 51998**) — a notice-date trigger in one place and an effective-date trigger in another.
2. **Between the Board and OPM**: OPM’s applicability turns on whether the agency **issued the specific RIF notice** on or after Sept. 2, 2026 (**2026-15666 DATES, 91 FR 49230**); the Board’s section III uses the **RIF effective date** (**91 FR 51998**). The Board’s DATES phrase “agency actions taken before the effective date” (**91 FR 51997**) is also ambiguous between notice issuance and RIF effectiveness.
Q14.uncertainty: The preamble-vs-text items are drafting inconsistencies; OPM may treat the regulatory text as controlling. The Board’s rule does not resolve whether the notice date or the RIF effective date controls for its retained cases.
